note: A blank field means nobody has verified it yet. It does not mean no. This matters most for hazards and dams.
sources: Lower Haw River State Natural Area

spots.name: Alligator River NWR, Milltail Road Launch
spots.hazards: Alligators, black bears and red wolves all present in this refuge. Do not approach wildlife. The canal system is extensive — carry a map and a compass as trails look similar. Blackwater canals can be disorienting. Cell service is extremely limited — one of the most remote areas on the East Coast. Download offline maps, charge your device fully, and tell someone your float plan before launching.
spots.notes_public: One of the wildest paddling destinations in the state. The refuge protects the largest intact tract of pocosin wetlands in the US and is home to one of the few wild red wolf populations in the world. Bears, alligators and red wolves all confirmed by visitors.
spots.cell_signal: Very limited. The refuge is one of the most remote areas on the East Coast. Most carriers lose signal in the interior. Download offline maps before you go and tell someone your plans.

spots.name: Anderson Point Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.parking_spaces: Small car park before the bridge, then a gravel road to the river
spots.restrooms: Yes, but three quarters of a mile to a mile away inside Anderson Point Park
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 16.2. The restrooms are a long walk from the water, so plan accordingly. Only 1.5 miles down to Poole Road, which makes this a short, easy pairing.

spots.name: Avalon Beach Boat Ramp
spots.hazards: Tidal sound waters. Currents stronger than they look, especially on a running tide. Wind builds quickly on open sound water. Check forecast before going out.
spots.notes_public: One of the most popular sunset spots on the OBX — reviewers call it a favourite for locals. Sound water access with decent parking. Good base for exploring Kitty Hawk Bay.

spots.name: Badin Lake Boat Ramp
spots.managing_agency: Alcoa Power Generating / Montgomery County Recreation
spots.restrooms: Portable toilet only, no trash cans on site
spots.notes_public: Badin Lake sits in the Uwharrie National Forest and is the most scenic flatwater in the Piedmont Triad region. The dock sits some distance from the ramps, so a second person on the boat helps with loading. Paddle north into wooded coves away from the ramp for the best scenery.

spots.name: Bald Head Island Ferry Access
spots.fee_permit: Ferry fare applies, currently about $30 round trip per person
spots.hours: Ferry runs daily, check schedule at baldheadisland.com
spots.motorized_allowed: No, the island is golf cart only
spots.hazards: Cape Fear inlet is one of the most powerful on the East Coast. Paddling directly to Bald Head from Southport is only for experienced coastal kayakers with knowledge of tidal currents. The ferry is the safe option for most.
spots.notes_public: A car-free barrier island with 14 miles of undeveloped beach and the oldest lighthouse in NC, Old Baldy, built in 1817. No cars allowed on the island. The Dutchman Creek ramp is the put-in for experienced paddlers making the crossing.

spots.name: Bass Lake Park
spots.managing_agency: Town of Holly Springs Parks and Recreation
spots.notes_public: A small 50 acre lake with a two mile loop trail around it. Rentals do not include boards, so bring your own.
spots.rentals: Canoes and rowboats, plus a Gheenoe with a trolling motor. Hirers must be 16 or over. Seven days a week from Memorial Day to Labor Day. No paddleboards listed.

spots.name: Beatty's Bridge Access, Black River
spots.walk_to_water: Steep path down the south bank just west of the bridge. Carry your boat down.
spots.parking_spaces: Roadside parking just west of the bridge
spots.hazards: Informal access with steep bank. Not suitable for motorboats. Fallen logs and strainers appear seasonally and are not mapped.
spots.notes_public: The take-out for the classic Ivanhoe run and the gateway to Three Sisters Swamp, where the second oldest known living tree in the world grows. Access is informal — a steep sandy bank west of the bridge with roadside parking. The Nature Conservancy has protected land along this stretch.

spots.name: Beatty's Ford Access Area
spots.parking_spaces: Large lot with room for long trailers
spots.restrooms: Yes, plus a playground and water play area
spots.notes_public: A hidden gem on the south-western arm of Lake Norman, consistently rated cleaner and less crowded than Blythe Landing. Four wide launch lanes, a playground, picnic areas and a water play area make it a full family outing. No staging dock, so having a partner in the boat for loading helps.

spots.name: Big O's Landing
spots.parking_spaces: Plenty, with room to turn a trailer
spots.restrooms: None. No toilets and no bins.
spots.notes_public: A well built, gentle ramp onto Lake Hickory with generous parking. No facilities at all, and paddlers consistently describe a litter problem. Fine as a put-in, less good as a place to linger.

spots.name: Black Bear Landing
spots.parking_spaces: Plenty, though it fills before midday on fine weekends
spots.hazards: Lake James is a hydroelectric reservoir, so the level rises and falls with power generation. Expect the shoreline and your take-out to look different from one visit to the next.
spots.notes_public: The biggest launch complex on the north side of Lake James, six ramps wide. Open around the clock and busy with trailers, so an early start is worth it. The approach road is winding.

spots.name: Blythe Landing Park
spots.fee_permit: Launch fee applies. Season passes available.
spots.notes_public: A busy trailer ramp with 218 trailer spaces, so expect motorboats. The nonprofit sailing centre on site is the interesting part for paddlers, offering the cheapest membership route onto this lake.
spots.private_launch: Yes for private boats. Only county-approved hire companies may launch commercially.
spots.rentals: Lake Norman Community Sailing, a nonprofit sailing centre, runs from here and its family membership covers kayaking and paddleboarding as well as sailing.

spots.name: Bob Perry Road Boat Ramp
spots.water_body: Jean Guite Creek / Kitty Hawk Bay
spots.launch_type: Wide single lane ramp with courtesy dock, plus a hand-carry kayak dock
spots.parking_spaces: 18 paved trailer spaces plus additional parking, picnic tables and grills
spots.ada_launch: Yes, NCWRC lists this as universally accessible
spots.hazards: Tidal sound waters. Currents stronger than they look, especially on a running tide. Wind builds quickly on open sound water. Check forecast before going out.
spots.notes_public: Gateway to Kitty Hawk Woods Coastal Reserve. Paddle north through Jean Guite Creek into the reserve's maritime forest and marsh, or south to reach Kitty Hawk Bay. Local outfitters run guided tours north to a covered bridge and south through an atoll to a mini-cape on state land.

spots.name: Boone's Cave Park, Yadkin River Access
spots.notes_public: A scenic and historically significant park on the Yadkin River. Named for the cave where Daniel Boone allegedly sheltered as a young man — the cave is accessible via stairs from the river trail. Multiple trails including the Cottonwood Trail leading to a 125-year-old cottonwood tree six feet wide at the base.

spots.name: Brices Creek Recreation Area
spots.managing_agency: US Forest Service, Croatan National Forest
spots.ada_launch: Yes, handicap accessible parking
spots.notes_public: The put-in for the Brices Creek Canoe Trail in the Croatan National Forest. Reviewers describe it as a beautiful and quiet spot to paddle with stunning views. Snakes are common — water moccasins and copperheads both sighted.

spots.name: Brooks Bridge Paddle Access
spots.hours: Gates are locked at closing. Seasonal hours, roughly 8am to 6pm November to March and later in summer.
spots.hazards: A low head dam sits at this access. Low head dams create a recirculating current below them that is extremely difficult to swim out of. Stay well clear of the face and below it.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes. Paddlers specifically warn about the dam here.
spots.notes_public: The top of the Haw River Paddle Trail and the first point the river is paddleable, with a small waterfall and an island. Quiet, often empty. The dam here deserves real respect.

spots.name: Brown Mountain Beach Resort
spots.camping_type: Cabins, cottages and yurts rather than pitches
spots.hazards: Wilson Creek is a designated Wild and Scenic river with real whitewater upstream. Class rises sharply after rain.
spots.notes_public: Not a public access, so this is one for a night away rather than a day trip. Guests get free use of kayaks, boards and tubes on the creek. Included because Wilson Creek has very little public paddler infrastructure and this is the practical way onto the gentle water.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, paddleboards, floating docks and tubes provided free to guests

spots.name: Buffaloe Road Canoe Launch
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.walk_to_water: Short, but paddlers describe the bank as steep and awkward for getting a boat in.
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Steep entry bank. Paddlers report Class I water just below the put-in, which makes paddling back upstream to the car impractical. Plan a downstream take-out.
spots.notes_public: River mile 10.7. Only about five parking spaces. The current just below the launch means this works as a put-in rather than an out-and-back.

spots.name: Burch Station / Elkin River Access
spots.restrooms: Y, bathrooms sometimes locked. Showers available at Yadkin Valley Heritage and Trails Visitor Center at 257 Standard Street weekdays 9am to 5pm.
spots.camping_type: Primitive camping allowed, no designated sites
spots.notes_public: The main access at Elkin on the upper Yadkin, gateway to Surry County which has more developed river access points than any other county in North Carolina. Primitive camping allowed. The 6.1-mile float to Donnaha passes through wine country foothills.

spots.name: Bynum Dam Access, US 15-501
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Bynum Dam. Put in above the dam only. Never approach a dam face from upstream.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes, Bynum Dam sits immediately downstream of this put-in
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Flat for about a mile upstream of the dam, which makes this the gentlest water on the Lower Haw. Stay above the dam.

spots.name: Bynum Mill Access
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: 160 Bynum Church Road. This is the only developed, official paddle launch State Parks maintains in the whole state natural area. Everything else here is undeveloped.

spots.name: Cahooque Creek Landing
spots.managing_agency: US Forest Service, Croatan National Forest
spots.ada_launch: Yes, reviewers describe handicap access
spots.notes_public: Where Hancock Creek and Cahooque Creek converge before joining the Neuse River. MCAS Cherry Point is nearby so expect F/A-18s overhead — actually a draw for some paddlers. Road in is rough and not recommended for heavy trailers.

spots.name: Cane Creek Park Lake
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, RV hookups and tent sites plus cabins
spots.notes_public: Not to be confused with the OWASA Cane Creek Reservoir in Orange County. This is Union County's lake near Waxhaw, and it is a very different experience: swimming allowed, paddleboards for hire, camping, disc golf, playgrounds and a mountain bike trail. Residents 65 and over get a free lifetime entry pass.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, in the designated swim area
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks, paddleboards and pedal boats

spots.name: Cane Creek Reservoir
spots.fee_permit: Orange County residents and OWASA customers: about $6 first person, $2.50 each additional adult, children under 12 and seniors $1. Non-residents: about $10 first person, $4 each additional adult. Private boat launch included in the lake use fee.
spots.hours: Fridays and Saturdays only, 6:30am to 6pm, late March through late October. Closed all other days.
spots.dogs_allowed: No pets within 50 feet of the lake
spots.notes_public: The largest body of water in Orange County and the number one birding hotspot in the county. Strict rules because it is a drinking water reservoir: no paddleboards, no swimming, no body contact with the water at all, no pets near the shoreline, and open only two days a week. Kayaks and canoes are fine and the water is exceptionally clean.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and all bodily contact with the water are prohibited.
spots.private_launch: Yes, kayaks and canoes only. Paddleboards explicitly prohibited.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and flat-bottomed boats available for hire on site

spots.name: Carbonton Access, Deep River
spots.managing_agency: Deep River Riverkeepers / Piedmont Legacy Trails
spots.launch_type: Former dam site — parking area with river access
spots.hazards: McIver Landing take-out has steep banks and is easy to miss from the water. Mark the take-out with a flag before launching. Check USGS gauge before going — river levels vary significantly.
spots.notes_public: Former site of the Carbonton Dam, now removed as part of the Deep River dam removal program. A parking area remains where river access is allowed. The La Grange Riparian Reserve — a Triangle Land Conservancy property of 308 acres dating to the 1700s — begins 1.4 miles downstream and extends 2.6 miles.

spots.name: Carolina Beach State Park
spots.camping_type: Drive-in with full hookups, cabins and primitive sites
spots.hazards: Cape Fear River currents and maritime traffic at the marina. Tidal waters. Currents stronger than they appear. Check tide tables and plan accordingly.
spots.notes_public: Home to the Venus flytrap in its only native habitat in the world. The marina sits on the ICW with a boat launch and kayak rentals available as early as 7am. Miles of flat trails through maritime forest.

spots.name: Carolina Beach Wildlife Boat Ramp
spots.hazards: ICW and inlet currents. Adjacent to Snow's Cut, Masonboro Island and the open ICW. Tidal waters. Currents stronger than they appear. Check tide tables and plan accordingly.
spots.notes_public: Put-in for Snow's Cut to the west, the southern tip of Masonboro Island to the north, or the Intracoastal Waterway to the east. A versatile launch for experienced coastal paddlers.

spots.name: Carova Beach Park and Boat Ramp
spots.hazards: Accessible only by 4WD on beach sand or by boat — no paved road access. Standard 2WD vehicles will get stuck. Sound conditions can be rough — check weather before launching. Wild horses are protected — maintain distance and never feed them.
spots.notes_public: A remarkable and remote park at the northern tip of the Outer Banks. 4.8 stars across 253 reviews. The dock was completely redone for 2026.

spots.name: Cedar Point Wildlife Ramp, White Oak River
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with dock and fishing pier
spots.hazards: Strong tidal current through the ICW channel — time your paddle with the tide. Exposed dock bolts noted by reviewers. Ramp angled slightly flat — take care at low tide.
spots.notes_public: NCWRC boating access at the mouth of the White Oak River where it meets the Intracoastal Waterway, near Emerald Isle. Separate fishing dock away from the ramp. Clean and well-kept facility near the Emerald Isle bridge.

spots.name: Concord Church Boating Access
spots.ada_launch: Yes, NCWRC lists as universally accessible
spots.notes_public: NCWRC universally accessible ramp on the South Yadkin River in Davie County. Clean, well-maintained access road noted by reviewers. Quiet and scenic.

spots.name: Copperhead Island
spots.notes_public: A 14 acre island park across the water from McDowell Nature Preserve. Quiet in the morning, busier once the trailers arrive. Six tent sites make it one of very few paddle-and-camp options this close to Charlotte.

spots.name: County Line Boating Access, Catawba River
spots.hazards: Strong current in the tailrace below Cowans Ford Dam when generation is occurring — do not paddle directly below the dam. Check Duke Energy's generation schedule before launching. Some sharp rocks near the ramp — watch boat hull.
spots.notes_public: NCWRC ramp at the base of Cowans Ford Dam on the Catawba River — the county line between Gaston and Lincoln counties. 4.7 stars across 23 reviews. Direct access to the tailrace below the dam — current can be strong when generation is occurring.

spots.name: Cross Point Landing
spots.notes_public: The quieter of the two Wildlife Commission ramps, at the opposite end of the lake from Holleman's Crossing. Plenty of room to manoeuvre.

spots.name: Deep River Park
spots.notes_public: A 40 acre park straddling the Chatham and Lee county line, run by a volunteer association and kept up by the Cumnock community. The historic Camelback Truss Bridge is on the National Register and you can sit on it and watch the river. A clean, easy landing, which paddlers rate more highly than the put-in at Gulf upstream.
spots.access_type: Private park, open to the public

spots.name: Deep River Park, Gulf Access
spots.hazards: River levels vary with rainfall. Check USGS gauge before launching. Dress for water temperature, not air temperature.
spots.notes_public: A quiet beginner-friendly access on the lower Deep River near Gulf. Mild current, easy takeout, small playground. Reviewers describe a smooth clean landing after floating from the canoe access upstream.

spots.name: Donnaha Park River Access
spots.parking_spaces: Good parking, can fill on summer weekends
spots.hours: 5am to 10pm Friday and Saturday, 6am to 9pm other days
spots.hazards: E. coli levels frequently fail swimming safety standards at this access per reviewer reports. Check Swim Guide before any water contact. The bridge overhead is covered in bird nests which likely contributes.
spots.notes_public: Popular Yadkin County river park on the protected stretch below Pilot Mountain State Park. The 8-mile section from East Bend River Park downstream is a favorite scenic float — bald eagles sighted regularly in this corridor. Small picnic shelter and bathroom.

spots.name: Dram Tree Park Boat Ramp
spots.hazards: Strong Cape Fear River currents and heavy maritime traffic. This is not a beginner paddling route. The river is wide and tidal — plan around the tide. Cargo vessels and large ferries use this stretch. Tidal waters. Currents stronger than they appear. Check tide tables and plan accordingly.
spots.notes_public: Downtown Wilmington's primary public boat ramp, under the Cape Fear Memorial Bridge. Scenic views of the USS North Carolina battleship across the river. The Cape Fear here is a working river — experienced paddlers only.

spots.name: Draper Boat Landing, Dan River
spots.hazards: Reviewers report the access has been gated and closed at times with no prior notification — verify before driving out. The ramp approach is steep in places.
spots.notes_public: NCWRC boating access on the Dan River near Eden. Important: reviewers report the access has been gated and closed without notice — call ahead or check the NCWRC access map before making the drive. When open, it provides a concrete ramp to the Dan River for flatwater paddling downstream toward Kerr Lake.

spots.name: Duck Town Park Soundside Launch
spots.hazards: Tidal waters. Currents run stronger than they look and change direction with the tide. Check tide tables and paddle on a rising or slack tide when possible. Wind can build quickly on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: A boardwalk park along the Currituck Sound with a soundside kayak launch, maritime forest and marsh trails, a playground and picnic shelters. Recommended by OBX guides as one of the most beginner-friendly sound launches. The boardwalk connects to shops and restaurants.

spots.name: Dutchman Creek Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Three single ramps with a separate T-dock
spots.parking_spaces: Good on regular days, crowded on holidays
spots.hazards: Access to the back side of Bald Head Island and the Cape Fear inlet. Strong tidal currents at the inlet and heavy maritime traffic in the channel. Not suitable for inexperienced coastal paddlers. Tidal coastal waters. Check tide tables and weather before launching.
spots.notes_public: Put-in for the back side of Bald Head Island via the ICW. Clean and well maintained, with a separate passenger drop-off dock. Southern hospitality noted in multiple reviews — strangers help each other launch and nobody blocks others in.

spots.name: Eaton Ferry Marina
spots.hours: Monday to Thursday 9am to 5pm, Friday to Saturday 9am to 7pm, Sunday 9am to 5pm
spots.notes_public: Lake Gaston sits on the Virginia line and is 34 miles long. Eaton Ferry is the primary public-access marina on the NC side, popular with families for pontoon rentals. Not a paddler-focused launch — pontoon and ski boat traffic is heavy — but the only practical entry on this end of the lake without a trailered boat.
spots.rentals: Pontoon boats, ski boats and fishing boats. Military discount available.
spots.access_type: Private marina, open to the public

spots.name: Edenhouse Bridge Boat Launch, Chowan River
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with fishing pier
spots.ada_launch: Yes, handicap parking available
spots.hazards: Launches directly into the open sound with no wind barrier. Check weather before launching — conditions can deteriorate quickly on the Albemarle Sound.
spots.notes_public: A well-maintained NCWRC ramp and fishing pier on the Chowan River just south of its confluence with Albemarle Sound. 4.6 stars across 33 reviews. Clean restrooms, handicap parking, fishing pier.

spots.name: Endless River Adventures
spots.fee_permit: Guided trips and rentals require booking. Prices on website.
spots.hours: Check website for current seasonal hours.
spots.hazards: The Cheoah River is Class IV+ whitewater on scheduled releases only — for advanced paddlers exclusively. Check American Whitewater for the release calendar before visiting. The Nantahala is Class II-III. Water is cold year-round. Dress for immersion.
spots.notes_public: A specialty kayak instruction and outfitting center near the Nantahala and Cheoah rivers. Known for quality instruction from beginner through advanced. The Cheoah River, released from Santeetlah Dam, is one of the most celebrated advanced kayaking runs in the Southeast — scheduled releases only.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes, inflatable kayaks. Shuttle service. Specializes in kayak instruction for all levels.

spots.name: Eno River Access at Red Mill Road
spots.notes_public: Off Red Mill Road near Teknika Parkway in eastern Durham County. Deep flatwater, described as the most accessible launch on the Eno. Two miles upstream to the Little River confluence, two miles down to Falls Lake.

spots.name: Eno River Boat Launch, Red Mill Road
spots.launch_type: Ramp with a new floating dock installed 2022
spots.hazards: Muddy and slippery bank when wet. Use the dock rather than the bank. Road access has had construction detours — check current routing.
spots.notes_public: Flatwater in both directions and genuinely board-friendly. Paddle two miles upstream to the Little River confluence at Penny's Bend or two miles downstream into Falls Lake. Water is deep along most banks.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Cabelands Access
spots.hours: 8:30am. Closes 30 minutes before park closing time.
spots.hazards: Swift and often shallow. The river drops one class when levels fall. Downed trees and log jams move with floods and are not always where maps show them.
spots.notes_public: The shortest walk to the Quarry, a popular swimming hole. The gorge section here is rocky and tight — the river is called Cabe's Gorge at this stretch and it rewards a scouting walk before committing to a run. Closed temporarily after flooding events; check before travelling.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Cole Mill Access
spots.hazards: Rapids appear above roughly 2.25 ft on the Eno gauges.
spots.flow_low_cfs: Below 3 ft on the Eno gauges runs shallow
spots.flow_high_cfs: Above 5 ft is beyond most paddlers' ability to self rescue
spots.notes_public: Six miles of trail and a Cole Mill Road gauge nearby, so you can check the level for this exact stretch before driving out.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Cole Mill Access
spots.hours: Cole Mill opens at 9am. Closes 30 minutes before park closing time.
spots.hazards: Swift and often shallow. The river drops one class when levels fall. Downed trees and log jams move with floods and are not always where maps show them.
spots.notes_public: Six miles of trail and the easiest hiking in the park. The Bobbitt Hole swimming hole is reachable from here. Storm damage closed parts of the trail and the suspension bridge as of late 2025 — check current conditions with the park office before travelling.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Fews Ford Access
spots.hazards: Rapids appear above roughly 2.25 ft on the Eno gauges. Swift and often shallow.
spots.flow_low_cfs: Below 3 ft on the Eno gauges runs shallow, harder in a canoe than a kayak
spots.flow_high_cfs: Above 5 ft the river leaves its banks and moves beyond most paddlers' ability to self rescue
spots.notes_public: Visitor centre access with the largest trail network in the park. The park itself describes the Eno as swift but often shallow, which makes paddling here level-dependent rather than reliable.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Pleasant Green Access
spots.parking_spaces: Gravel lot for about 10 to 15 cars, fills quickly at weekends
spots.hours: 8:30am. Closes 30 minutes before park closing time.
spots.hazards: Swift and often shallow. The river drops one class when levels fall. Downed trees and log jams move with floods and are not always where maps show them. The dam at this access was removed, ending the flatwater pool. The river now runs freely and has more current than it did before the removal. Paddling here is no longer suitable as a flatwater out-and-back.
spots.notes_public: Primarily a trail access point rather than a paddling launch since the dam removal. The Laurel Bluffs Trail runs from here, connecting to Pump Station and Cabelands. The parking lot entrance is a sharp right turn immediately after the bridge when travelling from the north — easy to miss.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Pump Station Access
spots.hours: 8am. Closes 30 minutes before park closing time.
spots.hazards: Swift and often shallow. The river drops one class when levels fall. Downed trees and log jams move with floods and are not always where maps show them.
spots.notes_public: The eastern end of the park, with access to the ruins of Durham's first pump station built in 1887. Connects to the Laurel Bluffs Trail and the Mountains-to-Sea Trail. Parking is roadside only with no formal lot.

spots.name: Fair Bluff Boating Access Area, Lumber River
spots.hazards: Strong current — plan a downstream float with shuttle. Upstream paddling is very challenging. Blackwater visibility is low — watch for submerged obstacles.
spots.notes_public: A clean, quiet ramp in the small town of Fair Bluff with ample street parking. The Lumber River here is blackwater — tea-colored from tannins, stained but clean. Current is strong — reviewer notes it took 1.5 hours to paddle 2 miles upstream.

spots.name: Falkland Boat Ramp, Tar River
spots.hazards: Water moccasins reported in dead trees along the bank — watch carefully near the water's edge. Shooting range adjacent to the ramp — gunshots are audible.
spots.notes_public: A clean NCWRC ramp on the Tar River between Rocky Mount and Greenville. 4.4 stars across 23 reviews. Good parking and bank fishing.

spots.name: Falls Dam Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.parking_spaces: Car park with double spaces for trailers, plus ADA parking
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 0.25 and the top of the Blueway, right below the Falls Lake dam. It is 4.7 miles down to Thornton Road. Flow here depends entirely on what the dam is doing.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, B.W. Wells Campground
spots.walk_to_water: Sites 4 and 5 are roughly 300 yards in. Gravel roads mean you can wheel gear down.
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.restrooms: Yes, flush toilets, showers and charging points
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: Group camping under old, tall, well spaced trees, with shoreline fishing from the farther sites. Mostly out of the RDU flight path, which is not true everywhere on this lake. Site 5 is the furthest and has the best views.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Beaverdam Access
spots.notes_public: The park lists Beaverdam as non-gas boating, which is why it stays calm on a summer weekend. Accessible fishing and swim beach.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Highway 50 Access
spots.launch_type: Concrete ramp with a courtesy dock
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: Widely rated the best ramp on Falls Lake: gentle gradient, good grip even wet, and a courtesy dock. The dam dividing Beaverdam Lake from Falls Lake sits here. Note it does not open until 8am, which frustrates anglers wanting a sunrise start.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Rolling View Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, with water and 30 amp electric at many sites
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: The most complete access on the lake and the only one with board hire on the doorstep. Swim beach, fishing pier, playground, amphitheatre, and a direct connection to the Mountains-to-Sea Trail. Shady sites, many with a water view.
spots.rentals: A privately owned marina next door hires kayaks, canoes and paddleboards, and has a concession stand, slips and storage.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Sandling Beach Access
spots.launch_type: No boat ramp. Non-motorised craft launch from the beach.
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.restrooms: Yes, plus showers and changing rooms
spots.motorized_allowed: No, there is no ramp here
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: No ramp, which is exactly why it is worth knowing about. You can carry a board or kayak straight down to the beach with no trailer traffic anywhere near you. Life jackets are available to borrow, and there are picnic shelters, a playground and trails.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Shinleaf Access
spots.walk_to_water: Sites run from a short walk to about a mile down a wide gravel then natural path. A trolley or dolly is worth having.
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle at weekends and on holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Free for day use the rest of the year. Reported at about $7 a car.
spots.camping_type: Hike-in, no vehicles at the sites and no electricity
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.hazards: Not every day-use area at Falls Lake opens year round. Check the park's operating season schedule before travelling out of season.
spots.notes_public: Hike-in camping with easy water access, and campers are explicitly encouraged to bring kayaks, canoes and boards. No engine noise at the sites, only boats out on the lake. Pick a site at the end of a branch for space and privacy.

spots.name: Falls Reservoir Boat Launch
spots.hazards: The waterfall at the upstream end is beautiful but requires scouting. Falls Dam is at the downstream end — do not paddle past the marked boundary. Motorized boats are permitted but traffic is typically light on weekdays.
spots.notes_public: A genuine hidden gem in the Yadkin chain. Falls Reservoir sits between Narrows Dam and Falls Dam, surrounded by Uwharrie National Forest rather than the housing developments and golf courses that line the other Yadkin lakes. Narrow and winding, it paddles more like a river than a reservoir.

spots.name: Farmer Lake
spots.hours: Wednesday to Friday 7am to 7pm, Saturday 7am to 7pm, Sunday 1pm to 7pm. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
spots.notes_public: A beautiful, very quiet lake in Caswell County that paddlers describe as too big to cover in one visit. Staff are reported as helpful and safety-conscious. A birder's lake — Green Heron and Scarlet Tanager recorded here.
spots.rentals: Kayaks available for hire on site

spots.name: Fayetteville Boating Access, Cape Fear River
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with canoe access steps
spots.hazards: Multiple reviewers report vehicle break-ins in the parking lot, including smashed windows and theft from truck beds. Do not leave anything visible in your vehicle. Parking lot has limited lighting. Consider parking elsewhere and shuttling gear to the ramp. The ramp surface has been reported as buckled and partially submerged at higher water — check conditions before launching larger boats.
spots.notes_public: NCWRC boating access on the Cape Fear River in Fayetteville. 4.2 stars across 47 reviews. Concrete ramp with canoe access steps.

spots.name: Flanners Beach Campground
spots.hours: Seasonal, first week of March to last week of November
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, 41 sites with some electric hookups
spots.notes_public: An Army Corps campground on the Neuse River beach with three miles of hiking trails and direct river access for paddlers. Hurricane Florence destroyed the retaining wall and beach stairs, which have been partially restored. A hidden beach is reachable at the far end of the property.

spots.name: Fort Fisher State Recreation Area
spots.restrooms: Y, clean with a bath area for rinsing
spots.hazards: Ocean conditions. Rip currents possible. 4WD vehicles with permits allowed on the beach — paddlers entering from the ocean beach should be aware of vehicle traffic. The Cape Fear inlet is heavily trafficked by large vessels.
spots.notes_public: The southern end of Pleasure Island, free to enter, with an undeveloped beach and access to the Cape Fear River mouth and the Atlantic. Popular for surf fishing and beach driving with a 4WD permit. The river side offers calmer water away from the ocean surf.
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, ocean beach, surf fishing and swimming

spots.name: Fort Macon State Park
spots.dogs_allowed: No, not allowed on the beach
spots.hazards: Ocean conditions apply on the Atlantic side. Bogue Sound is calmer but tidal. Tidal waters. Currents run stronger than they look and change direction with the tide. Check tide tables and paddle on a rising or slack tide when possible. Wind can build quickly on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: A Civil War fort at the eastern tip of Bogue Banks with a lifeguarded ocean beach and 3 miles of trails. The Bogue Sound side offers calmer paddling water and access to marsh habitats. The fort itself has remarkable architecture — casemates converted into historical exhibits.
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, lifeguarded ocean beach in season

spots.name: Franklinville Park Access, Deep River
spots.managing_agency: Town of Franklinville / Deep River Riverkeepers
spots.launch_type: Bank access via park; low banks, easy entry
spots.hazards: Ramseur Dam portage required at mile 1.1 — exit river right. Class II rapid just below the dam. Check USGS gauge before launching.
spots.notes_public: Put-in on the Deep River State Trail, easily accessible from NC 22 at Franklinville Park. Banks are low and entry is manageable. Brooklyn City Park (1 mile downstream) can serve as an alternative put-in from Leonard Park Street.

spots.name: French Broad River Park
spots.hazards: Hurricane Helene caused major flooding across the French Broad watershed in autumn 2024. The vast majority of accesses have reopened but some amenities and river conditions changed. Check frenchbroadpaddle.com for current status before going.
spots.notes_public: A well-used riverside park and greenway access in Asheville. Good put-in for the urban Asheville section of the French Broad. Dog-friendly with a dog park, walking paths, bike trail connections and a labyrinth.

spots.name: Glenburnie Park Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Two concrete ramps with courtesy docks
spots.notes_public: Sits on a skinny section of the upper Neuse that is ideal for paddlers — narrower and calmer than the wide estuary below downtown. The park has disc golf, a playground, a dog park and picnic areas, plus a history as a WWII POW camp. Reviewers warn about snakes in summer.

spots.name: Glencoe Paddle Access
spots.hazards: The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: Sits beside the restored Glencoe mill village, with a walking trail and a well liked sunset view. Good upstream paddling to swimming holes cut into the banks over the years.

spots.name: Goldsboro Boating Access Area, Neuse River
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with new fishing dock
spots.notes_public: A clean and well-reviewed NCWRC ramp on the Neuse River in Wayne County. 4.7 stars across 26 reviews. A new dock was installed recently — good for both fishing and boat launching.

spots.name: Goose Creek State Park
spots.hazards: The Pamlico River is wide and tidal. Wind can build quickly across open water. Check weather before heading out.
spots.notes_public: A gem on the Pamlico River with a surprising sandy river beach, kayak launch from the primitive campground dock, boardwalks through wetlands, and rangers who have been spotted guiding students to find sharks teeth on the beach. Cabins are available. Well maintained and praised by regular visitors.

spots.name: Gorges SP, Frozen Creek Access
spots.hazards: The Horsepasture River drops 2,000 feet over 18 miles and has serious whitewater. The Toxaway crossing at the trail is manageable at around 2.75 ft on the Rosman USGS gauge but dangerous above that. Gorges receives over 80 inches of rain annually and rivers rise fast. The trails here were heavily impacted by Hurricane Helene and cleanup continues as of mid-2026.
spots.notes_public: Temperate rainforest at the NC-SC line with 26 waterfalls and access to part of Lake Jocassee. The Frozen Creek access is the trailhead for the Foothills Trail and the Canebrake Trail to the Toxaway River crossing. Not a paddling destination in the conventional sense — the whitewater here is for experts only.
spots.cell_signal: None at the far end of the park.

spots.name: Graham Paddle Access
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, and paddlers report it is a friendly spot for dogs
spots.hazards: The boat ramp is reported to be very slick close to the water. The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: A plain access with no facilities at all, but a shady spot for lunch. Staff clear the car park promptly at closing, so do not plan to linger.

spots.name: Great Bend Park
spots.hazards: Paddlers report broken glass on the trails, sharp drops to the water at several points, and poorly maintained access points. There is a dam here. The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: Several trails and a tranquil dam, but the park is not well kept and the water access points are the weakest part of it. Restrooms and trail maps at the car park.

spots.name: Greenfield Lake Boathouse
spots.managing_agency: City of Wilmington / Cape Fear River Watch
spots.hours: Wednesday to Sunday 11am to 5pm. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
spots.hazards: Alligators present and regularly sighted. Reviewers report two at a time, small and mid-size. They keep their distance but do not approach or feed them.
spots.notes_public: A mile-long cypress-lined lake ten minutes from downtown Wilmington, draped with Spanish moss. Described by multiple sources as one of the prettiest paddles in the city. No currents, no tides, no motor boats — genuinely beginner-friendly.
spots.rentals: Single kayaks, tandem kayaks, paddleboards, canoes and paddleboats. Operated by Cape Fear River Watch.

spots.name: Greenville Town Common Boat Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Greenville Parks and Recreation
spots.ada_launch: Yes, accessible kayak and canoe launch installed 2018
spots.notes_public: The classic put-in for the 3.5-mile flatwater paddle to Port Terminal. Downtown Greenville's 21-acre riverside park, with an amphitheatre, inclusive playground and the Sycamore Hill Gateway Plaza. Motorized boats are directed to Port Terminal.

spots.name: Hamilton Boat Access Ramp, Roanoke River
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with floating dock
spots.hazards: Sand and silt buildup on the ramp below the waterline makes boat trailers tilt when loading — the ramp needs dredging. Check water level before arriving. Floating dock has been pushed toward the bank by current.
spots.notes_public: A quiet town ramp in Hamilton on the lower Roanoke River. Parking is adequate and the setting is peaceful — reviewers describe it as serene for fishing and clearing your mind. Note: significant sand and silt buildup on the submerged ramp surface causes boat trailers to tilt when loading — the ramp needs dredging.

spots.name: Hammocks Beach SP, Ferry Dock and Paddle Launch
spots.fee_permit: About $10 for the ferry, or paddle your own boat across for free
spots.restrooms: Y at mainland dock; shower house on Bear Island
spots.hours: Ferry runs seasonally. Check the park page for current schedule.
spots.motorized_allowed: No, paddlecraft to Bear Island only
spots.camping_type: Primitive island camping on Bear Island
spots.hazards: Open water crossing of the Intracoastal Waterway. Wind and boat wakes can make this challenging. Check conditions and tide before paddling over rather than taking the ferry. Strong currents in the inlet.
spots.notes_public: Bear Island is one of the most pristine undeveloped barrier island beaches on the East Coast. You can take the ferry for about $10 or paddle your own kayak or SUP across the Intracoastal Waterway — a genuinely achievable paddle of under a mile in calm conditions. Primitive camping on the island.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, Bear Island has an undeveloped ocean beach
spots.swim_area_here: No, swim beach is on Bear Island across the water

spots.name: Hanging Rock SP, Dan River Access
spots.notes_public: Dedicated paddling access on the Dan, linked to the main park area by the Indian Creek Trail.

spots.name: Hannah Ferry Road Boat Ramp
spots.hazards: Multiple reviewers report safety concerns at this access — no lighting, no signage from the road, muddy parking lot, and reports of needles and litter at the ramp. Scout the access before committing to a night or early morning paddle here. Consider using Boone's Cave or York Hill instead.
spots.notes_public: NCWRC access on the Yadkin between Boone's Cave and York Hill. Included for completeness as it appears on the Yadkin River State Trail map, but reviewer feedback raises consistent safety concerns — no lights, no road signage, poor lot condition, and litter. Boone's Cave Park upstream and York Hill downstream are both better maintained alternatives for most paddlers.

spots.name: Hap Simpson River Access Park
spots.hazards: Hurricane Helene caused major flooding across the French Broad watershed in autumn 2024. The vast majority of accesses have reopened but some amenities and river conditions changed. Check frenchbroadpaddle.com for current status before going.
spots.notes_public: Take-out for the classic Westfeldt to Hap Simpson run, 5.5 miles downstream. Shaded picnic tables, paved access and river overlook. Restrooms not confirmed on site — reviewers say no trash bags or poop bags so bring your own.

spots.name: Harkers Island Public Boat Ramp
spots.hazards: Large shoal outside the last red marker makes return very difficult at low tide. Multiple reviewers watched boats run aground. Hug the channel markers carefully on return. Check the tide before planning your return. Tidal coastal waters. Check tide tables and wind forecast before launching. Currents stronger than they look on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: Gateway to Cape Lookout National Seashore and Core Sound. The pier is described by reviewers as offering arguably the best publicly accessible inshore fishing in NC. Ferries to Cape Lookout depart from near here.

spots.name: Harrellsville Boat Ramp, Chowan River
spots.notes_public: A quiet and uncrowded NCWRC ramp in a peaceful neighborhood on the Chowan River in Hertford County. 4.6 stars. Reviewers describe it as a nice spot for fishing and putting a boat in the water without the crowds.

spots.name: Harris Lake County Park
spots.managing_agency: Wake County Parks, Recreation and Open Space
spots.launch_type: Cartop launch for canoes, kayaks and paddleboards only
spots.walk_to_water: You must unload in the car park and carry your boat 150 yards to the launch. No parking at the water.
spots.fee_permit: None to launch your own boat
spots.motorized_allowed: No. Nothing with a trailer or a motor may launch from inside the park.
spots.notes_public: A 680 acre park on a peninsula of Harris Lake. Note as of early 2026 the cartop launch was closed for construction of a new kayak launch, with paddlers directed to the shore access in the powerline easement near the picnic area. Ring ahead.
spots.rentals: None in the park

spots.name: Headwaters Outfitters
spots.hazards: Hurricane Helene caused major flooding across the French Broad watershed in autumn 2024. The vast majority of accesses have reopened but some amenities and river conditions changed. Check frenchbroadpaddle.com for current status before going. Trips cancelled at 3ft on the Rosman USGS gauge.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 3 ft on Rosman gauge — trips cancelled above this level
spots.notes_public: The headwaters section of the French Broad out of Rosman — gentle, lively current with fast-moving shoals and river bends. Highly rated operation with staff handling put-in and take-out. Includes a coffee truck and tap room.
spots.private_launch: Customers only, via private river access 1 mile from shop
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks. Self-guided 3-hour and 4 and 7-hour trips on Tuesdays. River trips cancelled at 3ft on the Rosman USGS gauge.

spots.name: Hidden Cove Access
spots.parking_spaces: About 20 trailer-length spaces, and it fills quickly
spots.restrooms: Single vault toilet, no running water
spots.hours: 7am to 9pm, and reported to close seasonally over winter
spots.hazards: Lake James is a hydroelectric reservoir, so the level rises and falls with power generation. Expect the shoreline and your take-out to look different from one visit to the next. Paddlers also report the access closed outside the main season despite listings saying otherwise, so ring the park first.
spots.notes_public: Quieter than the other Lake James ramps because it is easy to drive past. Facilities are primitive but functional. Unlike most access areas here it has posted hours rather than being open around the clock.

spots.name: Holden Beach Public Boat Ramp
spots.parking_spaces: Limited free spaces fill by 5am on fishing tournament weekends. Paid parking nearby.
spots.hazards: Ramps are slippery and flanked by sharp metal and oyster beds. Reviewer specifically warned of serious injury risk from a small slip. Very steep at low tide. Beginners should use a different access. Tidal waters. Currents stronger than they appear. Check tide tables and plan accordingly.
spots.notes_public: Main public ramp on the Lockwood Folly River at Holden Beach. Charter boats dominate the free parking by 5am on tournament weekends. Ocean Isle Beach ramp is recommended as safer with more and free parking.

spots.name: Holleman's Crossing Boating Access
spots.notes_public: The main trailer ramp on Harris Lake and the launch point for fishing tournaments, so expect bass boats. Ample parking and deep water at the ramp.

spots.name: Huntsville Yadkin River Access
spots.notes_public: Remote access on the historic Shallowford Ford crossing of the Yadkin, used by settlers on the Great Wagon Road, Patriot militia in 1780, Cornwallis in 1781, and Stoneman's cavalry in 1865. The river here runs clear and scenic. Good put-in or take-out for the 10.8-mile float to Tanglewood.

spots.name: Hyco Afterbay Boating Access
spots.notes_public: A great NCWRC ramp on the Hyco Afterbay — separate from the main Hyco Lake, connected by a spillway. 4.8 stars. Reviewers praise it as a fantastic spot to launch a boat or fish.

spots.name: Ivanhoe Boating Access Area
spots.notes_public: The main put-in for the Black River, one of the most extraordinary paddling rivers in North Carolina. The river holds the oldest known trees east of the Rocky Mountains — ancient bald cypress in the Three Sisters Swamp, some more than 2,600 years old. Named an Outstanding Resource Water by the state in 1994.

spots.name: Jockey's Ridge SP, Soundside Access
spots.parking_spaces: About 27 spaces, fills early on summer mornings
spots.hours: See the park website — seasonal hours apply
spots.hazards: Water quality advisory active as of August 2026 — bacteria levels exceed state recreational standards at this access. Check NC DEQ before swimming. Tidal waters. Currents run stronger than they look and change direction with the tide. Check tide tables and paddle on a rising or slack tide when possible. Wind can build quickly on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: The soundside face of the tallest living sand dune on the Atlantic coast. One reviewer calls it their favourite place to kayak and snorkel on the OBX. Shallow, calm sound water perfect for beginners, with maritime forest and wetland trails behind the beach.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, though a bacteria advisory was posted as of August 2026
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, sound beach — but check current advisories before swimming

spots.name: Jones Lake State Park
spots.notes_public: The most accessible of the Carolina Bay lakes with full camping, kayak hire on site, a swim area kept separate from the paddling zone, and well-maintained facilities. Deeply loved — reviewers note low light pollution and excellent night skies from the campsite. Well suited to families.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, a designated swim area separate from the boats
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, swim area kept separate from the paddling and fishing
spots.rentals: Kayaks and canoes on site

spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Boat ramp and swim beach are for campers only. A privately owned marina sits nearby.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Privately owned marina nearby hires fishing boats, kayaks and paddleboards

spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Named by the park as the best access for windsurfing, which tells you it catches wind. Accessible swim beach and picnic shelters on site.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Day-use ramps plus short hike-in backpack camping. The quietest corner of the lake.

spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Tent, trailer and RV sites with some hookups, plus walk-up only loops and group camping. Swim beach and picnic shelters.

spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Campers-only boat ramp and docks. Walk-up loops mean you can sometimes get a site without booking.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.notes_public: Wide open view of the lake, which is scenic and also means very little shelter from wind.

spots.notes_public: Group camping only, both RV and tent. Sailboat launch and swim beach.

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, White Oak Recreation Area
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.hours: 9am to 5pm weekdays. Closed Saturday and Sunday.
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Open for day use in peak season only when the rental facility is not booked, so call ahead before driving out.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake, Farrington Point Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Four concrete ramps plus a separate hand-carry launch
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: The north end of the lake and the busiest tournament ramp on Jordan — nearly every bass tournament launches here because it is free and open around the clock. Four ramps for trailered boats on the right and a separate dedicated launch on the left for canoes and kayaks. Despite the tournament traffic, paddlers say waits rarely exceed ten minutes and are usually none at all.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, designated areas elsewhere on the lake
spots.swim_area_here: Small beach area, not a designated swim beach

spots.name: Jordan Lake, Poe's Ridge Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Two concrete ramps, one floating pedestrian dock
spots.parking_spaces: Car and trailer parking, limited car-only spaces
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.ada_launch: Yes, ADA accessible aluminum floating dock
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: At the south end of the lake near the dam, one of four 24-hour ramps on Jordan. The only one managed by the Army Corps of Engineers rather than NC State Parks or the Wildlife Commission. One lane is blocked by the pedestrian dock placement, so effectively one usable ramp.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, designated areas elsewhere on the lake

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Bullocksville Access
spots.notes_public: Accessible fishing pier, concession stand and a short hiking loop. No boat ramp listed by the park.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.parking_spaces: Two ramps with parking described as somewhat tight
spots.notes_public: Open sailing water with camping and group sites.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Henderson Point Access
spots.notes_public: Accessible fishing pier and a swim area. Good sailing water, which means it is open and can get choppy.

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Hibernia Access
spots.notes_public: Longest trail in the park runs from here, along with a swim area and group camping.
