spots.notes_public: Ramp and dock are campers only. Sits within the Satterwhite Point access.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Kimball Point Access
spots.notes_public: Swim beach and camping. Named by the park as good sailing water, so read the wind before you go.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Nutbush Bridge Access
spots.notes_public: Two ramps, one sized for fishing tournaments. Expect heavy trailer traffic on tournament weekends.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Satterwhite Point Access
spots.notes_public: Visitor centre, the park's only designated swim beach, and a privately owned marina. The busiest access on the lake.
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, the only designated swim beach in the park
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kinston Boating Access Area, Neuse River
spots.hazards: Very shallow and rocky near the ramp — not suitable for larger bass boats. Debris in the water noted by reviewers. No bathrooms on site.
spots.notes_public: NCWRC ramp on the Neuse River in Kinston. 4.5 stars across 47 reviews. Good views and a nice dock.

spots.name: Lake Benson Boat House
spots.managing_agency: Town of Garner Parks and Recreation
spots.dogs_allowed: No, pets are not permitted on boathouse craft
spots.notes_public: Worth reading twice before you drive out. You cannot put your own boat on this lake at all, only boathouse craft, and the boathouse opens weekends only. A shallow, quiet lake if you are happy in a hired kayak.
spots.rentals: Jon boats, kayaks and canoes from the boathouse. Trolling motor available.

spots.name: Lake Brandt Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
spots.fee_permit: Fishing permit required. Kayak and SUP rental fees apply.
spots.hours: Monday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday 7am to 8pm. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
spots.notes_public: One of three Greensboro city reservoir lakes with paddling access, and the most popular. 4.6 stars across 654 reviews. Beautiful lakeshore trails, fishing pier, and friendly staff.
spots.rentals: Single kayaks, tandem kayaks, canoes, paddleboards and jon boats. See marina for current rates.

spots.name: Lake Chatuge, Hiwassee Lake Access
spots.notes_public: Lake Chatuge is a 7,050-acre TVA reservoir straddling the NC-Georgia border near Hayesville in Clay County. The NC side of the lake is the quieter, more scenic portion — mountain views, clear water, and less development than the Georgia side. Good for flatwater kayaking and SUP.

spots.name: Lake Crabtree County Park
spots.managing_agency: Wake County Parks, Recreation and Open Space
spots.notes_public: Free boat hire, which is rare, and that includes paddleboards. Demand is heavy at weekends and in good weather, so paddlers advise arriving about half an hour before opening.
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks, rowboats, pedal boats and paddleboards, free of charge with valid ID

spots.name: Lake Devin
spots.launch_type: Boat ramp plus a separate dedicated kayak launch
spots.notes_public: A lake with two separate access points: a boat ramp and a dedicated kayak launch. Trails are described as overgrown and unmarked in places. A good birding lake — Loons, Grebes, Wilson's Snipe and ducks recorded here.

spots.name: Lake Higgins Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
spots.fee_permit: About $6 to $8 per private boat, depending which page you read. An annual launch pass is available. All boaters must register and pay at the marina office.
spots.hours: Seasonal, check the marina before setting out
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, there is a ramp for motorboats
spots.notes_public: At 226 acres this is the smallest and quietest of the Greensboro city lakes, with a hatchery pond and a shoreline trail. The gentler alternative when Brandt and Townsend are busy. Coordinates here are approximate and want checking on the ground.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and wading are prohibited at all Greensboro city lakes.
spots.rentals: Solo kayak about $15, tandem about $25, paddleboard about $15, canoe about $25. Higgins is the only one of the three city lakes that hires canoes. Hire runs 1 May to 31 October, first come first served, with no time limit. Renters must be 16 or over. Ages 9 to 15 may paddle a solo boat with a signed waiver and a parent alongside in another boat. Under 9 must share a tandem with an adult. These age rules apply to private boats too.

spots.name: Lake James SP, Catawba River Access
spots.walk_to_water: Campsites are a long walk from the car park, reported as up to a mile and downhill on the way in. Wheelbarrows are provided. The access road may not be used for unloading.
spots.restrooms: Yes, bath house at the car park
spots.hazards: Lake James is a hydroelectric reservoir, so the level rises and falls with power generation. Expect the shoreline and your take-out to look different from one visit to the next.
spots.notes_public: A 24-hour ramp and the easiest put-in for the Long Arm paddle-in campsites. You can boat right up to a lakefront site, and there are lockers at the sites for food. Pack light if you are walking in, because the haul from the car park is a real one.

spots.name: Lake James SP, Paddy's Creek Access
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, 33 sites with parking for two vehicles
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. No pets on the beach.
spots.hazards: Lake James is a hydroelectric reservoir, so the level rises and falls with power generation. Expect the shoreline and your take-out to look different from one visit to the next.
spots.notes_public: A rare thing in this dataset: a genuine sandy swim beach with a designated swimming area, backed by Blue Ridge foothills. Launch from the day-use area at the end of Lake James State Park Road for the paddle-in campsites on Long Arm peninsula, about a mile out. Take a free overnight parking pass for the dashboard and park in the top tier of the car park.
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, a large sandy swim beach
spots.rentals: Canoes and kayaks on site

spots.name: Lake Johnson Park
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks and Recreation
spots.walk_to_water: Paddlers report hauling boats from the far end of the car park when the near lot fills. Awkward with anything you cannot carry one-handed.
spots.parking_spaces: Two car parks, both of which fill early at weekends
spots.notes_public: A 150 acre lake close to NC State, calm and well liked by beginners. Parking is the real constraint. Arrive early at a weekend or you will be carrying your board a long way.
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards from WakeRack lockers by the Waterfront Center. Pedal boats, canoes and fishing boats through the park.

spots.name: Lake Lucas
spots.managing_agency: City of Asheboro Cultural & Recreation Services
spots.fee_permit: $3.00 with Asheboro Rec Card, $4.00 without. Kayak rental $6.00/$10.00 per day. Annual launch permit $35/$50.
spots.hours: March 1 to November 15: Monday to Sunday 7am to sunset, closed Wednesdays. November 16 to February 28: 8am to 5pm, closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, up to 15hp. No jet skis or personal watercraft.
spots.notes_public: A well-maintained 238-acre lake managed by the City of Asheboro. Reviewers describe it as spotless, quiet, and friendly — staff at the office are consistently praised. A quarter-mile walking trail runs past the dam.
spots.rentals: Jon boats ($10/$15 per day) and kayaks ($6/$10 per day), available 8am to 2pm daily during operating hours.

spots.name: Lake Lure, Washburn Marina Ramp
spots.fee_permit: Boat permits required — see 2026 Lake Use Fees at townoflakelure.com. Non-motorized vessels may launch at Pool Creek Picnic Park (2724 Memorial Hwy) without a permit.
spots.hours: Washburn Marina Ramp and Pool Creek picnic ramp open as of May 16, 2026. Lake Lure Beach open Memorial Day weekend through August 11, 2026. Check townoflakelure.com for current hours and permit requirements.
spots.hazards: Submerged debris and logs may still be present in some areas — paddle and boat with caution even after reopening. Depths and navigation markers have changed since Hurricane Helene. No wake restrictions were lifted May 19, 2026 but conditions remain variable. The dam's long-term replacement is still in planning — a 30% design project is underway with $484,471 in grant funding.
spots.notes_public: Lake Lure reopened to the public May 16, 2026 — one week ahead of schedule — after a 20-month closure caused by Hurricane Helene (September 2024). Helene deposited 1.1 million tons of sediment and debris into the lake, forcing the Army Corps of Engineers to drain it nearly completely for cleanup. The lake refilled to full pond by April 2026.

spots.name: Lake Mackintosh Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of Burlington Recreation and Parks
spots.hours: 7am to 7:30pm, to 8pm Saturday. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
spots.hazards: Paddlers report submerged stumps and floating logs and debris. Less of a problem on a board than under a propeller, but worth watching in the shallows.
spots.notes_public: The closest Triad lake to Chatham County and well liked by paddlers, with staff who will suggest a route and tell you the distance. Quiet enough that regulars are protective of it. Shoreline is zoned by activity.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and paddleboards

spots.name: Lake Michie Park and Marina
spots.ada_launch: Yes
spots.hours: 6:30am to 6pm Friday through Monday. Closed Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
spots.notes_public: One of the very few launches in the region with an ADA accessible boat house, dock and canoe/kayak launch. Non-motorized only, covering canoes, kayaks, paddleboards and sailboats, so it stays quiet.

spots.name: Lake Norman State Park
spots.notes_public: Largest manmade lake in the state with 520 miles of shoreline. Boat rentals, swim beach and cabins. Check the DEQ algal bloom dashboard here in summer.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Boat hire on site

spots.name: Lake Norman YMCA Lake Access
spots.hours: Lake access is seasonal and limited, historically summer Saturdays only. Ring before going.
spots.notes_public: A supervised cove with lifeguards on the water and life jackets required, which makes it one of the gentlest introductions to a board anywhere on Lake Norman. Equipment is free but you need a Y membership, and lake access hours are far shorter than the building's.
spots.private_launch: Members only. Nationwide YMCA memberships are accepted.
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks and paddleboards provided free to members, plus inflatables in the cove

spots.name: Lake Thom-A-Lex Park
spots.ada_launch: Yes, the launch is described as accessible
spots.notes_public: Shared by Thomasville and Lexington, hence the name. An accessible launch, trailer parking and a bait shop, with a lakeside walking trail and plenty of shoreline.

spots.name: Lake Townsend Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
spots.launch_type: Large boat ramp plus a separate ramp for small sailboats
spots.fee_permit: About $6 to $8 per private boat, depending which page you read. An annual launch pass is available. All boaters must register and pay at the marina office.
spots.ada_launch: No, but the fishing pier, parking and restrooms are reachable with a mobility device
spots.hours: 7am to 8pm. Closed Wednesday and Thursday. All boats off the water 30 minutes before closing.
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, there is a ramp for motorboats
spots.hazards: Closed two days a week.
spots.notes_public: Greensboro's largest municipal reservoir and home to the Lake Townsend Yacht Club, which is open to the public and does not require you to own a boat. Open sailing water, so read the wind. Bring your own board, since hire here is kayaks and rowboats only.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and wading are prohibited at all Greensboro city lakes.
spots.rentals: Solo kayak about $15, tandem about $25, and rowboats. No paddleboard hire listed here, unlike Brandt and Higgins. Sailboats can be hired with prior experience. Hire runs 1 May to 31 October, first come first served, with no time limit. Renters must be 16 or over. Ages 9 to 15 may paddle a solo boat with a signed waiver and a parent alongside in another boat. Under 9 must share a tandem with an adult. These age rules apply to private boats too.

spots.name: Lake Waccamaw NCWRC Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Double concrete ramps with large L-shaped floating dock
spots.notes_public: The public ramp for Lake Waccamaw, one of the most ecologically unique lakes on Earth. Despite its size the lake is only ten feet at its deepest, so only small craft are practical. Well maintained double ramps with a recently added L-shaped floating dock.

spots.name: Lake Waccamaw State Park
spots.hazards: Alligators are present. Do not feed them and keep a safe distance from the water's edge.
spots.notes_public: Lake Waccamaw is one of the largest natural lakes in North Carolina and one of the most ecologically unique — it has its own endemic species found nowhere else on Earth, including the Waccamaw killifish, silverside and mussel. Boardwalks over wetlands, wildlife in abundance including alligators, and calm, clear waters ideal for paddling. An underrated destination.
spots.swimming_allowed: No swimming allowed in the park

spots.name: Lake Wheeler Park
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks and Recreation
spots.launch_type: Ramp for trailered and hand-carried boats
spots.fee_permit: Daily or annual launch pass required, about $6 a day for non-residents
spots.hours: 6am to 8pm. Boats must be off the water 30 minutes before sunset or closing, whichever is first.
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, no jet skis. 40 mph limit, and skiing and tubing are permitted.
spots.notes_public: A 650 acre water supply lake, and the clearest example of flat water that is not swimmable. Swimming and wading are both banned, and motorboats can run at 40 mph with skiers behind them. Fine for a confident paddler, a poor choice for a first time on a board.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and wading are both prohibited.
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards from WakeRack self-service lockers near the Waterfront Center, booked online

spots.name: Latta Nature Preserve
spots.notes_public: Mountain Island Lake is smaller and far less trafficked than Lake Norman, with much less motor traffic. Forested and undeveloped, and a good choice when the big lake is churned up.
spots.rentals: Mountain Island Lake Paddle Company will deliver boards and kayaks to the launches

spots.name: Leaksville Landing, Dan River
spots.managing_agency: City of Eden Parks and Recreation
spots.notes_public: A pleasant river access in downtown Eden with steps directly to the Dan River. Reviewers describe it as a great spot for photos, relaxing on the bank, and skipping rocks. The river is wide and calm here, good for kayaking downstream.

spots.name: Lillington Boating Access Area, Cape Fear River
spots.launch_type: Primitive boat ramp — canoe and kayak suitable
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes but shallow and rocky — kayak/canoe recommended
spots.hazards: Primitive and muddy ramp — not suitable for larger power boats. Shallow and rocky near the ramp. Heavy trash along the shoreline. River levels vary significantly — check before going.
spots.notes_public: A primitive NCWRC access on the Cape Fear River in Lillington. 4.4 stars across 19 reviews. Good for canoe and kayak launch — reviewers describe nice trails down to the water and good fishing.

spots.name: Lilly's Bridge Marina
spots.hours: Tuesday to Thursday 10am to 4pm, Friday 10am to 4pm, Saturday 10am to 5:30pm, Sunday 12:30 to 5:30pm. Closed Monday.
spots.notes_public: A full-service marina on the south arm of Lake Tillery with a restaurant, mini-golf and a boat ramp open to the public. Rated the favourite launch on the lake by regular paddlers. Closed Monday.
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboard hire, plus pontoon boats. Restaurant on site.
spots.access_type: Private marina, open to the public

spots.name: Little River Fishing Facility
spots.hours: 6:30am to 6pm Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Closed Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
spots.notes_public: Rental only, like Lake Benson. You cannot launch your own boat here, and it is shut three days a week. Restrooms on site, no bait sold.
spots.private_launch: No. Hired craft only, and private trolling motors are not permitted.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and jon boats with trolling motors. Bring your own battery.

spots.name: Long Island Road Boat Ramp, Catawba River
spots.ada_launch: Yes, handicap parking available
spots.notes_public: A well-regarded NCWRC ramp on the Catawba River with two concrete ramps and a center dock. 4.4 stars across 70 reviews. Handicap parking available.

spots.name: Lookout Shoals Boat Ramp
spots.hazards: Boat traffic on weekends. Trash littering reported — watch for fishing line and debris near the ramp.
spots.notes_public: A peaceful NCWRC ramp on Lookout Shoals Reservoir between Lake Norman and Lake Hickory. 4.7 stars across 41 reviews. Good for kayaking and bank fishing.

spots.name: Lumber River SP, Chalk Banks Access
spots.notes_public: The Lumber is a Wild and Scenic river and one of the darkest blackwater rivers in the Southeast — tannin-stained and deeply remote. Chalk Banks is the main access on the upper river, with picnic grills and a riverside trail. No swimming due to snags, currents and the remoteness.

spots.name: Lumber River SP, Princess Ann Access
spots.restrooms: Y, clean pit toilets and water faucets
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, walk-in group, and paddle-in sites
spots.hazards: River levels vary significantly. At very low water, fallen trees are uncovered and may require portaging. Wire Pasture access is closed until further notice due to illegal activity — confirm you are heading to Princess Ann or Chalk Banks, not Wire Pasture. Bug spray is essential, especially in summer.
spots.notes_public: The main access for the Lumber River, North Carolina's only National Wild and Scenic blackwater river. Griffin's Whirl, a rare reverse-flow section of the river below the bluff, is directly accessible from here. Paddle-in camping on sandy beaches.
spots.cell_signal: Limited. Very rural Robeson County, spotty coverage.

spots.name: Manteo Waterfront Public Boat Ramp
spots.parking_spaces: Limited — no trailer parking in the lot
spots.hazards: Tidal waters. Currents run stronger than they look and change direction with the tide. Check tide tables and paddle on a rising or slack tide when possible. Wind can build quickly on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: Right on the Manteo waterfront with views of the Elizabeth II replica ship and Roanoke Marshes Light. The lot takes cars without trailers — if you have a trailered boat there is nowhere to park. Best suited to cartop launches.

spots.name: Mayo River SP, Anglin Mill Access
spots.notes_public: Mayo Beach and the Boiling Hole are here. No restrooms, so plan around that.

spots.name: Mayo River SP, Mayodan Access
spots.notes_public: Put in on the Mayo and paddle down into the Dan.

spots.name: McDowell Nature Preserve
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, small RV area with electric and water
spots.notes_public: One of the few Mecklenburg sites that explicitly welcomes your own board, launching from the landing by the waterfront deck. Nature centre, forested trails and quiet lake views.
spots.private_launch: Yes, bring your own canoe, kayak or paddleboard
spots.rentals: None for hire, but guided programmes provide boats

spots.name: Medoc Mountain State Park
spots.notes_public: The park calls this one of the cleanest streams in the region. Quiet paddling with almost no boat traffic.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Merchants Millpond State Park
spots.notes_public: One of the finest paddling destinations in North Carolina, full stop. A blackwater millpond under a canopy of bald cypress and tupelo gum draped with Spanish moss — one reviewer called it his favourite park for over 30 years and noted the cell service is essentially nonexistent. No motors, no crowds, no glamping.
spots.cell_signal: Very limited. Essentially no cell service in most of the park.

spots.name: Milton Boating Access Area, Dan River
spots.notes_public: A quiet NCWRC ramp in the small historic town of Milton, Caswell County — one of the oldest towns in NC and home to Thomas Day, the famous 19th-century free Black furniture maker. The Dan River here is broad and slow, good for flatwater paddling. Very limited reviews but those available are positive.

spots.name: Morrow Mountain State Park
spots.notes_public: Sits where Lake Tillery meets the Yadkin, under the Uwharrie peaks. Boat rentals on site and bald eagles overhead.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Boat hire on site

spots.name: Mt Holly Boat Landing
spots.managing_agency: Privately owned, Aquatic Adventures operates from here
spots.fee_permit: About $2 per person to launch a boat, canoe or kayak
spots.hazards: Sits just below the Mountain Island Lake dam. Flow changes when the dam releases.
spots.notes_public: Private land, and worth every bit of the two dollars. Just south of the Mountain Island dam on a wide, quiet stretch. The run downstream is about 2.75 miles through tree-lined water with almost no development or boat traffic.
spots.private_launch: Yes, for a small per person fee
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards on site. Aquatic Adventures runs guided trips and full moon paddles from here.

spots.name: NC Hwy 49 / Tuckertown Reservoir Ramp
spots.parking_spaces: Large gravel lot, accommodates many boat trailers
spots.hazards: Tuckertown Reservoir — ten minutes by water to the main channel. Motorized boats dominant on weekends. Water levels vary with dam operations. Algae noted in reviews during summer months.
spots.notes_public: The ramp you spotted on Highway 49. Two concrete ramps on Tuckertown Reservoir, which sits between High Rock Dam upstream and Tuckertown Dam downstream. About ten minutes by water to the main channel.

spots.name: NC Wildlife Beaufort Boating Access
spots.launch_type: Two concrete ramps with courtesy docks
spots.hazards: Tidal coastal waters. Check tide tables and wind forecast before launching. Currents stronger than they look on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: The main public ramp in Beaufort, along Taylor Creek with views across to the Rachel Carson Coastal Reserve. Paddle across Taylor's Creek to the Reserve, where a herd of feral horses lives on Carrot Island. Continue south 2.7 miles to Shackleford Banks for wild horses, an ocean beach, and one of the most iconic paddles on the Crystal Coast.

spots.name: NC Wildlife Blounts Creek Boating Access
spots.hazards: Tidal and wind-driven currents in the Pamlico River and Sound. Check weather before launching — the open water can become rough quickly.
spots.notes_public: A clean and well-maintained NCWRC ramp on Blounts Creek near its confluence with the Pamlico River. 4.6 stars across 32 reviews. Reviewers consistently praise it as not crowded, clean, and great for ramps.

spots.name: Nantahala Outdoor Center (NOC)
spots.fee_permit: Guided trips and rentals require booking and payment. See noc.com.
spots.hours: Open daily 8am to 8pm. Hours vary seasonally — check noc.com.
spots.camping_type: On-site lodging, cabins, and camping available.
spots.hazards: The Nantahala Gorge section is Class II-III with one Class IV rapid at Nantahala Falls near the takeout. Water releases from the bottom of Nantahala Lake and stays 45-55 degrees F year-round regardless of air temperature. Dress for immersion — hypothermia risk even in summer. Beginners should use guided trips only.
spots.notes_public: The Nantahala Outdoor Center is one of the most celebrated paddling destinations in the Southeast — 4.7 stars across 5,293 reviews. The 8-mile Nantahala Gorge run ends with Class IV Nantahala Falls. Water is crystal clear and cold year-round.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes, rafts, stand-up paddleboards. Guided trips and self-guided rentals with shuttle service available.

spots.name: Nantahala River Launch Site, Topton
spots.managing_agency: US Forest Service / Nantahala National Forest
spots.launch_type: River launch site with parking, restrooms, and historical kiosk
spots.hours: Open during daylight hours. Restrooms open seasonally (April 1 to November).
spots.hazards: Water is 45-55 degrees F year-round regardless of air temperature — dress for immersion, not the air temp. Upper section Class I-II; gorge section Class III with Class IV Nantahala Falls near the NOC take-out. No gas or services nearby in winter.
spots.notes_public: A beautiful and well-kept Forest Service recreation area at the upper Nantahala River. 4.8 stars across 133 reviews. Grounds are clean, peaceful, and surrounded by trees with a scenic creek and small walking bridge.

spots.name: Neuse Adventures
spots.notes_public: A well-reviewed outfitter on the Neuse between Falls Lake and Smithfield. Staff handle put-in and take-out, making it a good option for a first river trip. Paddlers consistently mention wildlife — beavers, kingfishers, herons.
spots.rentals: Canoes and kayaks with shuttle service. Two-hour and five-mile float options.

spots.name: New River SP, Elk Shoals Access
spots.restrooms: None at the access, chapel nearby
spots.notes_public: The only access on the New River with a swim beach and the most popular in summer. Shallow, clear water excellent for families with young children. Gate occasionally closed without notice — reviewers report driving out to find it shut.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, Elk Shoals has a sandy beach swim area

spots.name: New River SP, Kings Creek Access
spots.notes_public: Parking access for the Alleghany paddle-in only campground downstream. Reviewers call this their favourite campsite on the river, with primitive sites directly on the water. The Alleghany access itself is reachable only by canoe or kayak from here.

spots.name: New River SP, US 221 Access and Visitor Center
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, RV hookups and primitive sites
spots.notes_public: The main visitor centre and one of the two primary car-launch accesses on the New River. The river here is shallow, gentle Class I, ideal for beginners and families. The park covers 26.5 miles of one of the oldest rivers on Earth — more than a billion years old, older than the Appalachian Mountains that surround it.
spots.swimming_allowed: Yes, at Elk Shoals access area
spots.swim_area_here: No, swim beach is at Elk Shoals

spots.name: New River SP, Wagoner Road Access
spots.walk_to_water: Sites vary. Hand carts provided to move gear to riverside sites.
spots.notes_public: The second primary car-launch, eight miles southeast of Jefferson. Hand carts are provided at the campground for gear transport to riverside sites. Paddle-in campsites available from here.

spots.name: Newport River Pier and Ramp
spots.launch_type: Six concrete ramps with courtesy docks
spots.ada_launch: Yes, wheelchair accessible approach confirmed by reviewers
spots.hazards: Tidal coastal waters. Check tide tables and wind forecast before launching. Currents stronger than they look on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: The largest public ramp in the Morehead City area with six lanes and 54 trailer spaces. Fishing pier alongside. 4.6 stars across 273 reviews.

spots.name: Oak Hollow Marina
spots.managing_agency: City of High Point Parks and Recreation
spots.camping_type: Large campground, over 100 RV sites with hookups and some tent spaces
spots.notes_public: The most developed lake in the Triad, with a campground, golf course, sailing club and an open air stage. It also permits water skiing, so the wake is real. Swimming is not allowed.
spots.rentals: Kayaks solo and tandem, paddleboards and sailboats

spots.name: Ocean Isle Beach NCWRC Boat Ramp
spots.parking_spaces: Generous, recommended over Holden Beach for ease
spots.hazards: Tidal coastal waters. Check tide tables and weather before launching.
spots.notes_public: The Brunswick Islands' most recommended public ramp — better sheltered from wind and current than Holden Beach, easier to manoeuvre, and free. Paddlers looking at Holden Beach are directed here by reviewers. Seafood restaurants within walking distance.

spots.name: Old Bynum Bridge Access
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Parking on the east side of Bynum Road. Downstream from here to US 64 is rated by the state natural area for intermediate to advanced paddlers only.

spots.name: Oregon Inlet Fishing Center
spots.restrooms: Y, plus gas, snacks and tackle on site
spots.hazards: Oregon Inlet is one of the most dangerous inlets on the East Coast. Strong tidal currents, shifting sandbars and ocean swells make this unsuitable for paddlers except those with significant open-water coastal experience. Tidal sound waters. Currents stronger than they look, especially on a running tide. Wind builds quickly on open sound water. Check forecast before going out.
spots.notes_public: A full-service marina adjacent to the Bonner Bridge, with a charter fishing fleet and a view of Bodie Island Lighthouse. The inlet itself is hazardous for small craft. Included for completeness as the main southern OBX sound access, but paddlers should use the sound side ramps further north rather than launching into the inlet.
spots.access_type: Private marina, open to public for ramp use

spots.name: Oriental Boat Access Area
spots.hazards: Exposed to Pamlico Sound — conditions can deteriorate rapidly with wind. Check weather before launching. Strong currents when wind-driven.
spots.notes_public: NCWRC boat ramp in Oriental — known as the 'Sailing Capital of North Carolina' and one of the most charming small towns on the NC coast. 4.7 stars. Access to the Neuse River estuary and Pamlico Sound.

spots.name: Pea Island NWR Boat and Kayak Launch
spots.hazards: Tidal waters. Currents run stronger than they look and change direction with the tide. Check tide tables and paddle on a rising or slack tide when possible. Wind can build quickly on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: A low-key launch onto the Pamlico Sound at Pea Island National Wildlife Refuge. Reviewers describe it as a hidden gem — easy entry, excellent wildlife, and rarely busy. No facilities at all, so plan accordingly.

spots.name: Pee Dee River Blueway Boat Launch, Rockingham
spots.launch_type: Boat ramp with walking path to river
spots.notes_public: A clean and pretty Pee Dee River Blueway access point in Rockingham. 4.7 stars from a small number of reviewers. Short walk from the parking area to the river.

spots.name: Penrose Boating Access Area, French Broad River
spots.launch_type: Floating dock and ramp, canoe launch, universally accessible
spots.ada_launch: Yes, universally accessible per NCWRC
spots.hours: CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE — Hurricane Helene flood damage
spots.hazards: CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE due to Hurricane Helene flood damage (October 2024). Verify reopening with NCWRC before visiting: ncwildlife.gov/boating. The French Broad upper section has Class I-II rapids. Water is cold year-round — dress for immersion.
spots.notes_public: NCWRC universally accessible boating access on the upper French Broad River at river mile 32.5, nestled between Pisgah National Forest and DuPont State Recreational Forest. A floating dock, ramp, gravel parking, and kiosk with trip information make this one of the most complete small access points on the French Broad Paddle Trail. Popular take-out for day trips on the upper French Broad.

spots.name: Perquimans Boat Ramp, Hertford
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp — recently remodeled and enlarged
spots.ada_launch: Yes, recently remodeled with improved access
spots.hazards: The channel leading to the ramp has silted in significantly — only about 1.5 feet of water reported at low water. Jet skis and small motorized boats have gotten stuck. Check water levels before launching anything larger than a kayak.
spots.notes_public: Recently remodeled and enlarged NCWRC ramp on the Perquimans River in Hertford. 4.7 stars. Parking area was expanded in the renovation.

spots.name: Pettigrew State Park, Lake Phelps
spots.notes_public: Lake Phelps is one of the oldest and deepest natural lakes in North Carolina and is described by regular visitors as a hidden gem. The park is the third least visited in the state system. Water levels were significantly down in the 2026 drought — check with the park before making the trip.

spots.name: Pilot Mountain SP, Ivy Bluff Access
spots.walk_to_water: Roughly half a mile of trail from the car park down to the river. Smooth surface and a gradual slope, but a long way with a hard board or a canoe on your shoulder.
spots.notes_public: Parking for paddle-in campers, with steep riverside slopes on the hiking approach.

spots.name: Pilot Mountain SP, Shoals Fishing Area
spots.notes_public: Paddling launch for the Yadkin, doubling as a fishing access.

spots.name: Pine Hall Boating Access Area
spots.notes_public: One of the most praised public ramps on the Dan River. Reviewers call it the best public launch they have ever used — exceptionally clean, well-maintained, and free. Two concrete ramps with dock.

spots.name: Piney Bluff Boat Launch
spots.parking_spaces: Good parking, though it fills at busy times
spots.notes_public: The main launch on Belews Lake, north of Winston-Salem and Greensboro. Popular with jet skis and party boats, so pick your day. Open around the clock.

spots.name: Pinnacle Yadkin River Access
spots.notes_public: NCWRC boating access on the Yadkin River near Pilot Mountain. This section of the Yadkin runs through the protected corridor below Pilot Mountain State Park — one of the most scenic stretches of the river. Gateway to the Class I-II paddle between Pinnacle and Donnaha through the Yadkin's most wildlife-rich corridor.

spots.name: Pireway Boating Access Area, Lumber River
spots.hazards: Blackwater — low visibility below the surface. Remote location with limited cell signal. Alligators present in this section of the Lumber River — keep dogs and children away from the water's edge.
spots.notes_public: A quiet NCWRC ramp in southern Columbus County on the lower Lumber River — one of the few designated Wild and Scenic Rivers in North Carolina. The blackwater river here is tea-colored from tannins, stained but clean. Very few reviews but those available praise the kind people and good fishing.

spots.name: Poole Road Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.parking_spaces: Car park with double spaces for trailers
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 17.7 and the downstream end of the Raleigh section. A gravel road just before the river bridge leads in.

spots.name: Port Terminal Boat Access
spots.ada_launch: Yes, dedicated ADA-accessible kayak launch added 2023, built by Sound Rivers
spots.notes_public: The downstream take-out for the classic 3.5-mile Greenville Town Common to Port Terminal flatwater paddle. Old-growth trees line the banks with shifting sandbars that appear seasonally. Only twenty minutes by motorboat to Washington NC's waterfront.

spots.name: Radio Island Beach Access
spots.hazards: Hand carry kayak and SUP only — no motorized boats. Tidal current in the Bulkhead Channel. Tidal coastal waters. Check tide tables and wind forecast before launching. Currents stronger than they look on open sound water.
spots.notes_public: A calm, protected beach on Radio Island, the small strip of land on US 70 between Morehead City and Beaufort. Ideal for beginners and families. Kayaking, SUP, and swimming in flat sheltered water.

spots.name: Ramseur Lake
spots.hours: Wednesday to Friday 7am to 8pm, Saturday 7am to 8pm, Sunday 8am to 7pm. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
spots.notes_public: A quiet town lake on a branch of the Deep River, with improved docks and a fishing pier. Staff described by reviewers as friendly and attentive. No pets allowed, which one reviewer found listed as dog-friendly online and then discovered was wrong on arrival — worth confirming before bringing dogs.
spots.rentals: None confirmed

spots.name: Ramseur Lake Access, Deep River
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp and kayak launch
spots.hours: Wednesday to Sunday 7am to 8pm (closed Monday and Tuesday)
spots.notes_public: Town-managed lake and park with a dedicated kayak and canoe launch. Free parking. Calm flatwater — good for beginners and families.

spots.name: Ramsey Creek Park
spots.ada_launch: No, but there is an ADA compliant fishing pier
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, there is a dog park at the entrance
spots.notes_public: A seasonal lifeguarded beach, four ramps and a dog park. The shoreline is rocky, so water shoes help. Check beach dates before relying on it.

spots.name: Randleman Regional Reservoir Marina
spots.fee_permit: Ramp fee applies, staffed check-in station
spots.hours: 6am to 8pm. Closed Monday and Tuesday. Paddlers report it often opens nearer 7am.
spots.notes_public: A large, relatively new drinking water reservoir with good fishing. Tightly regulated: no swimming, no entering the water, closed two days a week and crowded at weekends. Flat and paddleable, but not a lake to fall into by choice.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Entering the water at all is prohibited, as this is a drinking water reservoir.

spots.name: Raven Rock State Park
spots.notes_public: The park explicitly names rapids on the Cape Fear here, plus the remains of the Northington Lock and Dam. Scout before you run it and check the class rating against current flow.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: River Bend Park Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.parking_spaces: Car park with double spaces for trailers, plus ADA parking
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 10, and the best equipped access on the Blueway. Restrooms and a changing area, which none of the others have. Only a mile down to Buffaloe Road.

spots.name: River Falls Park and Boat Ramp, Weldon
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with walking path and dock
spots.hours: Open daily — check town website for seasonal hours
spots.hazards: Class I-II rapids at the fall line — approach carefully at higher flows. Rapids can disappear entirely when upstream dam releases are high. Check flow before paddling this section.
spots.notes_public: A scenic and historic park at the fall line of the Roanoke River — the upper limit of navigation and home to the famous Weldon rockfish run. 4.6 stars across 332 reviews. Walking path leads to a dock with beautiful views of the river.

spots.name: River Park North
spots.managing_agency: City of Greenville Parks and Recreation
spots.fee_permit: None for trails and river access. Fishing requires a permit. $2 donation for some programmes.
spots.camping_type: Primitive river-access sites plus drive-to sites
spots.notes_public: An 18-acre park on the Tar with fishing ponds, nature trails, a science centre and paddle boats on the ponds. River access connects to the Tar-Pamlico Water Trail. Three primitive camping platforms on the river, closed in summer due to insects near the swamp — ring ahead.
spots.swimming_allowed: No, not recommended in the river

spots.name: River Road Park
spots.launch_type: Single concrete ramp plus a kayak and paddleboard launch
spots.hazards: Cape Fear River currents and maritime traffic. Tidal waters. Currents stronger than they appear. Check tide tables and plan accordingly.
spots.notes_public: One of the best-rated launches near Wilmington. A separate kayak and SUP launch sits alongside the main ramp. Good shark tooth hunting on nearby Shark Tooth Island accessible by paddle.

spots.name: Roanoke Island Festival Park Kayak Launch
spots.fee_permit: Free to launch from the floating dock. Museum admission separate.
spots.hours: Tuesday to Saturday 9am to 5pm, Sunday 1pm to 5pm. Closed Monday.
spots.hazards: Tidal sound waters. Currents stronger than they look, especially on a running tide. Wind builds quickly on open sound water. Check forecast before going out.
spots.notes_public: A floating dock launch on the northwest edge of the park, described by OBX paddle guides as tapping into a canal that connects to Shallowbag Bay. Paddle south past the Elizabeth II replica ship and Roanoke Marshes Lighthouse. A secluded beach on state land sits halfway to Pirate's Cove — a good rest stop.

spots.name: Roanoke Rapids City Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp — no fishing allowed, launching only
spots.notes_public: City-managed boat ramp on Roanoke Rapids Lake. 4.4 stars. Convenient and well-maintained.

spots.name: Roanoke River Boardwalk and Boat Ramp, Williamston
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with floating dock, handicap accessible boardwalk
spots.ada_launch: Yes, handicap accessible boardwalk and ramp
spots.camping_type: Shelter campsite on site with keypad entry (manual key backup available)
spots.notes_public: A beautifully maintained riverside facility with boardwalk, boat ramp, fishing areas, and a campsite shelter. 4.7 stars across 79 reviews. Handicap accessible.

spots.name: Robertson Millpond Preserve
spots.managing_agency: Wake County Parks, Recreation and Open Space
spots.launch_type: Loading dock for canoes, kayaks and boards
spots.fee_permit: None to launch your own boat
spots.hazards: Shallow stretches that are awkward on a board, and water levels drop noticeably in drought.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes, the historic mill dam. The pond is deeper near it.
spots.notes_public: The only blackwater cypress swamp in Wake County and quite unlike anything else near Raleigh. A marked paddling trail loops in about an hour, mixing open water with tight passages through the cypress. Some sections are shallow enough to be tricky on a board.
spots.rentals: Kayak hire on Saturdays only

spots.name: Robeson Creek Boat Ramp
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: A full trailer ramp run by the Wildlife Resources Commission, so expect motorboats. Paddle about a mile down Robeson Creek to reach the Haw.

spots.name: Robeson Creek Canoe Access
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Despite the name this launch is on the Haw, not on Robeson Creek. Flat for a short way upstream and flat for a long way downstream all the way to Jordan Lake, which makes it the best board-friendly put-in on the Lower Haw.

spots.name: Rodanthe Boating Access Area
spots.hazards: Open Pamlico Sound. Wind builds quickly and can make return paddle very difficult. Check forecast. This is an exposed sound-side access. Tidal coastal waters. Check tide tables and weather before launching.
spots.notes_public: Sound-side access at Rodanthe on Hatteras Island, giving directly onto the Pamlico Sound. Adjacent to Pea Island NWR. Reviewers describe easy entry and beautiful, wildlife-rich paddling.

spots.name: Salem Lake Marina Center
spots.managing_agency: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
spots.restrooms: Yes, ADA compliant at the marina and part way round the trail
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, up to 60 horsepower. No jet skis and no pleasure boating.
spots.notes_public: Over 350 acres inside the city limits, and the horsepower cap plus the jet ski ban make it far calmer than its size suggests. A seven mile dirt trail rings the lake.
spots.rentals: Boat hire from the marina centre, which also holds the fishing station and bait shop

spots.name: Saxapahaw Lake Paddle Access
spots.launch_type: Dock, with a life jacket loaner station
spots.walk_to_water: Carry your boat from the car to the dock, then park in the main lot or at the Boy Scout camp nearby. Short carry, described as very manageable.
spots.notes_public: Flat water behind the old mill dam, which makes this the gentlest put-in on the whole Haw and the one to pick for a first river paddle or a low water summer day. Out-and-back paddling with herons, egrets and a beaver dam. Walking trails, a playground and food within a short walk, plus a kayak shop nearby.

spots.name: Shallow Ford Natural Area
spots.launch_type: Paddle boat slip from a gravel car park
spots.walk_to_water: A second access sits down the Homestead Trail with a steep climb down to the water. Wear proper shoes and think twice with a hard board.
spots.hours: Gates are locked at closing. Seasonal hours, roughly 8am to 6pm November to March and later in summer.
spots.hazards: Fast flowing water and a steep bank at the trail access. The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: Multiple river access points, several miles of well marked trail and primitive camping, on a section of the Mountains-to-Sea Trail. One of the few Haw accesses where you can stay the night.
spots.swimming_allowed: Not advised. Paddlers describe the river here as muddy and fast flowing.

spots.name: Silver Lake Harbor, Ocracoke
spots.hazards: Ocracoke is only accessible by ferry from Cedar Island, Swan Quarter or Hatteras. Pamlico Sound is wide open water — conditions can change rapidly and are not suitable for inexperienced paddlers in windy weather. Tidal waters. Currents stronger than they appear. Check tide tables and plan accordingly.
spots.notes_public: The harbour at Ocracoke Village, one of the most historically rich and remote communities on the Outer Banks. A genuine destination paddle — the sound side of the island is protected and beautiful. Plan ferry times carefully as they must be booked in advance especially in summer.

spots.name: Singletary Lake State Park
spots.camping_type: Group camp and cabin rentals only, reserve well in advance
spots.notes_public: One of the Carolina Bay lakes — a chain of elliptical wetland lakes formed by a still-debated geological process unique to the Atlantic coastal plain. Singletary is the largest Carolina Bay lake in the state parks system. The interpretive signage on the boardwalk between the dock and the bridge is exceptional — one reviewer called it the best educational trail they had encountered in any state park.
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, swimming dock on the lake

spots.name: Smithfield Town Commons
spots.route_name: Neuse River Blueway, Johnston County section
spots.notes_public: One of only two established Neuse accesses in Johnston County, the other being near Richardson Bridge at Princeton. A riverside park with a paved path, in the town centre. Smithfield is the start of the 170 mile Mountains-to-Sea paddle route to the Croatan.

spots.name: Snow Hill Wildlife and Boat Launch, Contentnea Creek
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with fishing pier and walking trails
spots.notes_public: A NCWRC wildlife area and boat launch on Contentnea Creek in Greene County. 4.3 stars across 40 reviews. Wooded trails for walking dogs, fishing pier, picnic area.

spots.name: Soundside Park, Surf City
spots.managing_agency: Town of Surf City Parks and Recreation
spots.launch_type: Boardwalk and dock access to the sound
spots.hazards: Tidal current in the ICW channel. Check tides before launching — the sound is calm near the park but the main channel has current. Motorized boat traffic in the ICW.
spots.notes_public: A beautifully maintained sound-side park in Surf City with boardwalk, fishing pier, playground, and direct access to Topsail Sound. 4.8 stars across 1,196 reviews — one of the highest-rated parks on the entire NC coast. The boardwalk gives paddlers a great place to stage a launch onto the calm sound side, away from ocean surf.

spots.name: South Bynum River Access
spots.walk_to_water: Long. The recommended approach is to park on the east side of the historic Bynum Bridge and walk across it, which is a real haul with a canoe or a hard board.
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Formerly Bynum Beach Canoe Access. Parking is extremely limited and roadside parking on Bynum Beach Road is expressly prohibited, so plan on the bridge walk with your board.

spots.name: South Mountains SP, Clear Creek Access
spots.hazards: Reported closed for construction of a new car park from 31 March 2026, possibly until the end of the year, with no parking and no trespassing signs posted. Confirm with the park office before travelling.
spots.notes_public: A day-use access on Clear Creek with a pond, picnic area and restrooms at the trailhead, and a trail running beside the water. Shallow in places. Check it has reopened before you make the drive.

spots.name: Southmont Abbotts Creek Boat Access
spots.notes_public: High Rock is the second largest lake in the state and, unusually for this region, has a designated swim area elsewhere on the water. Paddlers rate this access as markedly less crowded than Norman or Wylie, with shoreline fishing and walking trails.

spots.name: Spring Garden Landing Boat Ramp
spots.launch_type: Single concrete ramp with courtesy dock
spots.notes_public: The northernmost Neuse access in Craven County, connecting to a moderately wide and relatively quiet section of the river above the busier downtown stretches. Good put-in for longer upstream paddles.

spots.name: Stone Mountain State Park
spots.camping_type: Drive-in with hookups and primitive sites
spots.notes_public: A spectacular granite dome rising 600 feet above the surrounding terrain — one of the most visited state parks in NC. The Roaring River runs through the park with trout fishing and creek paddling. No cell service in most of the park.
spots.cell_signal: No cell service in most of the park.

spots.name: Sunset Beach Boat Access
spots.hazards: Tidal coastal waters. Check tide tables and weather before launching.
spots.notes_public: Listed by Brunswick Islands tourism as a specifically designed kayak, canoe and SUP launch site. The town sits at the western end of the Brunswick Islands, with marsh creeks and the ICW accessible from here. A fishing pier is adjacent.

spots.name: Sunset Park Boat Ramp
spots.hours: 1pm to 7pm Monday to Friday, 1pm to 7pm Saturday, 1pm to 5pm Sunday
spots.route_name: Tar River Paddle Trail, Upper Tar section
spots.hazards: Davenport grist mill dam sits about 1.25 miles downstream from the Reservoir Dam access upstream. Portage on river right. The dam area is private property — stay in the boat.
spots.notes_public: One of the Upper Tar section access points on the Tar River Paddle Trail, which connects 55 miles of river across ten launches. From here downstream the Tar becomes increasingly flatwater. Tar River Life in nearby Bunn offers kayak rentals and shuttle services if you need them.

spots.name: Sutton Lake Boating Access
spots.launch_type: Dual concrete ramps with a dedicated kayak launch and chute
spots.hazards: Alligators present and getting bolder according to reviewers — one reported an alligator getting noticeably closer each visit. Do not feed wildlife. Mercury advisories posted for fish. Do not eat fish from this lake.
spots.notes_public: Solar-powered lights at the ramps make early morning and evening launches practical. A dedicated kayak chute sits alongside the dual boat ramps. Excellent access but the approach road has significant potholes.

spots.name: Swepsonville River Park, Lower Access
spots.hours: Gates are locked at closing. Seasonal hours, roughly 8am to 6pm November to March and later in summer.
spots.hazards: The shallow rocky sections make good rapids at normal level but are hard work when the river is low. The stretches backed up behind old mill dams stay paddleable in a dry summer.
spots.notes_public: Calm water and a good put-in. From the lower access you can run downstream toward Saxapahaw or turn up Great Alamance Creek. Popular with bank anglers, so the parking goes quickly.

spots.name: Swift Island Access Area
spots.notes_public: A quiet Wildlife Commission ramp on Lake Tillery with a boardwalk and family-friendly shoreline. Reviewers describe a peaceful Sunday-afternoon feel with trucks and trailers but enough room to move. One of the calmer ends of a large lake.

spots.name: Tailrace Marina
spots.notes_public: Near the mouth of Dutchman's Creek where it meets Lake Wylie. Online booking and waivers mean you can be on the water quickly. A long-standing Catawba Riverkeeper Riversweep site.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, paddleboards, canoes and pontoons. An annual kayak membership covers a guest.

spots.name: Tanglewood River Access
spots.hazards: Portage required at Idol's Dam approximately 4 miles downstream. Exit river right just before the railroad trestle. Do not miss this — the dam is dangerous at all water levels.
spots.notes_public: Hand-carry access via gravel ramp and natural steps. Gateway to a scenic section of the Yadkin through Forsyth County. Trail access from the parking area.

spots.name: Tar River Reservoir Boat Ramp
spots.route_name: Tar River Paddle Trail, Nash County section
spots.notes_public: Free 24-hour ramp at the upper reservoir. A quiet, remote flatwater stretch above the main Rocky Mount section, with occasional motorboat traffic. Jacob's Swamp at river mile 93 is accessible by a small cut on river left.

spots.name: The Floatery
spots.fee_permit: Varies by trip type. Book and pay in advance.
spots.hours: Saturday and Sunday 8am to 4pm for bookings. Closed Monday to Friday.
spots.notes_public: One of the most distinctive outfitters in the state. Known for a 65-foot water slide into the river and an outstanding guided firefly float in June and the first week of July, when the trees along the river are full of fireflies. The night float runs 7:30 to 10pm and includes a guide, tracker, glowstick, headlamp, life jacket and shuttle — everything you need.
spots.rentals: Tubes, kayaks and paddles. Guided firefly float June through early July, 7:30pm to 10pm — includes tracker, glowstick, life jacket, headlamp, shuttle and guide. Day floats with a 65-foot water slide into the river. Cooler float option available. Staff carry your cooler to and from the water.

spots.name: Thelma Boating Access, Roanoke Rapids Lake
spots.launch_type: Paved boat ramp with floating dock and pole holders
spots.notes_public: A clean and peaceful NCWRC ramp on Roanoke Rapids Lake — the uppermost of the Roanoke chain of lakes below Kerr Lake. 4.6 stars across 67 reviews. Paved ramp, floating dock with pole holders.

spots.name: Thornton Road Access
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
spots.walk_to_water: Half a mile down the paved greenway. Carry your boat to the T junction, turn right and walk a short way further. A serious haul with a canoe or hard board.
spots.hours: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking, cars may not be left overnight.
spots.hazards: Fast current can push you into downed trees, log jams and bridge footings. The bed is uneven, so never stand where the water is deep enough to float you. Avoid the river in high flow.
spots.notes_public: River mile 4.5. The longest carry on the Blueway by a wide margin, so worth knowing before you load the car. Signs mark the access once you reach the greenway.

spots.name: Trails End Boat Ramp
spots.parking_spaces: 30 spaces, fills quickly on summer weekends
spots.hazards: Tidal ramp — low tide makes entry tricky. Docks deteriorating and have no cleats. Strong ICW currents when tide is running. Parking often taken by cars rather than trailers. Tidal waters. Currents stronger than they appear. Check tide tables and plan accordingly.
spots.notes_public: Gateway to Masonboro Island, one of the longest undeveloped barrier islands on the East Coast. Paddling to Masonboro across the ICW is achievable in calm conditions, about a mile. Masonboro Paddle Company and other outfitters meet customers here.

spots.name: U.S. National Whitewater Center
spots.fee_permit: Around $39 for a day of flatwater kayaking and paddleboarding, plus about $13 to park
spots.notes_public: The flatwater paddling here is on the Catawba and Long Creek and is separate from the artificial whitewater channel. Everything is an added fee, so read the pricing before you go.
spots.private_launch: Unknown, the site is built around its own hire fleet
spots.rentals: Flatwater kayaks and paddleboards included in the activity pass. Life jacket provided.

spots.name: US 64 Haw River Canoe Access
spots.parking_spaces: Large gravel lot at 348 River Access Road, plus a very small gravel lot on the south east side and roadside parking on the north west service road
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: The state natural area rates the run downstream of here for experts only.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Experts only heading downstream toward Robeson Creek. The classic Lower Haw whitewater run starts here and it is not a beginner stretch.

spots.name: Union Point Park Boat Ramp
spots.water_body: Neuse River at Trent River confluence
spots.launch_type: Two concrete ramps with courtesy dock
spots.parking_spaces: 8 paved boat trailer spaces plus street parking
spots.notes_public: Where the Neuse and Trent rivers meet beside historic downtown New Bern, NC's first state capital. The confluence makes for interesting flatwater paddling in multiple directions with wide river views, marshy edges and birdlife. Stillwater Kayaks operates nearby for rentals and gear.

spots.name: University Lake
spots.fee_permit: Orange County residents and OWASA customers: about $6 first person, $2.50 each additional adult, children under 12 and seniors $1. Non-residents: about $10 first person, $4 each additional adult. Private boat launch included in the lake use fee.
spots.hours: Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, 6:30am to 6pm, late March through late October.
spots.dogs_allowed: No pets within 50 feet of the lake
spots.notes_public: Smaller than Cane Creek and closer to Chapel Hill. Opens on Sundays unlike Cane Creek, which makes it the more accessible of the two for a weekend paddle. Same rules apply: no boards, no swimming, no pets at the shore.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and all bodily contact with the water are prohibited.
spots.private_launch: Yes, kayaks and canoes only. Paddleboards explicitly prohibited.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and flat-bottomed boats available for hire

spots.name: Uwharrie River Low Water Bridge Access
spots.managing_agency: US Forest Service, Uwharrie National Forest
spots.hazards: The low water bridge itself floods after heavy rain, sometimes impassably. Check before driving down the gravel road, which has no turnaround. River rises fast in the gorge.
spots.notes_public: The Uwharrie runs through a National Forest gorge with no development visible from the water. Paddlers report wide stairs from the parking area down to the river and room to splash around. The road in is gravel and the bridge floods — check conditions before driving out.

spots.name: Uwharrie River Public Fishing Area
spots.launch_type: Canoe and kayak launch at confluence with Yadkin River; fishing dock, handicap access patio
spots.ada_launch: Yes, handicap access patio for fishing
spots.hazards: Zero cell phone service in this area — download offline maps before going. Snakes reported in the area — watch carefully. Small feeder creek alongside the entry road floods after heavy rain.
spots.notes_public: A beautiful and quiet NCWRC fishing area and kayak/canoe launch at the confluence of the Uwharrie and Yadkin rivers. 4.6 stars across 37 reviews. Handicap-accessible fishing patio overlooking the confluence.

spots.name: Valdese Lakeside Park
spots.ada_launch: Yes, the ramp is wide enough for a manual wheelchair or a power scooter
spots.hours: 7am to 8pm, and to 11pm on Friday and Saturday
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, there is a fenced dog park and water at the gate
spots.notes_public: Lake Rhodhiss is the quieter, more intimate paddling water in Burke County, and this is the best entry to it. A waterfront boardwalk, a suspension bridge and about 12 miles of trail, with a view of Table Rock at sunset. One of only a handful of accessible launches in the whole dataset.
spots.rentals: RAD Rentals will deliver kayaks and paddleboards direct to the dock

spots.name: Washington Baum Bridge Boating Access
spots.parking_spaces: About 50 trailer spaces, very few car-only spaces
spots.hazards: Tidal sound waters. Currents stronger than they look, especially on a running tide. Wind builds quickly on open sound water. Check forecast before going out.
spots.notes_public: The most-referenced sound launch on Roanoke Island, directly under the Washington Baum Bridge. Roanoke Sound is described by multiple paddling guides as one of the best paddling environments on the OBX — protected water that rarely gets choppy, excellent wildlife, and the option to paddle toward Manteo's historic waterfront. Reviewers flag very limited car-only parking — come with a trailer or arrive very early.

spots.name: Watauga River Paddle Trail Access, Sugar Grove
spots.hazards: Class II-III whitewater — intermediate to advanced paddlers only. Water is cold year-round in the mountains. Dress for immersion. Check gauge before running — river rises quickly after rain.
spots.notes_public: Access point on the Watauga River Paddle Trail in Watauga County. 4.6 stars. Plenty of room and shallow enough for dogs to swim.

spots.name: Water Street Ramp, Plymouth
spots.launch_type: Concrete boat ramp with floating dock
spots.hazards: Tournament traffic on Saturdays March through November — check for events before planning a weekend launch. Tidal influence this close to Albemarle Sound — check tide tables.
spots.notes_public: A popular and well-reviewed ramp in downtown Plymouth with easy access to the Roanoke River and Albemarle Sound. 4.5 stars across 48 reviews. Parking is across Water Street behind the Port O' Plymouth Museum — a short walk but spacious.

spots.name: West Point on the Eno
spots.hazards: Mill dam at the historic mill. Put in above the dam.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes, the mill dam. Launch above it.
spots.notes_public: Enter above the dam behind the mill and paddle roughly three quarters of a mile up to Sennet Hole. The dam holds deep water year round, so this is one of the few Eno spots that does not depend on rain.

spots.name: Westfeldt Park
spots.hazards: Hurricane Helene caused major flooding across the French Broad watershed in autumn 2024. The vast majority of accesses have reopened but some amenities and river conditions changed. Check frenchbroadpaddle.com for current status before going.
spots.notes_public: Put-in for the most-paddled stretch in Henderson County, 5.5 miles of Class I to Hap Simpson Park in Fletcher. Lazy Otter Outfitters operates from here with single kayaks, tandem kayaks, SUPs and tubes, including a horseshoe bend 4-mile trip option. Check Helene recovery status.

spots.name: William B. Umstead SP, Crabtree Creek Access
spots.notes_public: Big Lake and Sycamore Lake, with boat rentals on site. Nine miles from downtown Raleigh and it feels much further.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Boat hire on site

spots.name: William B. Umstead SP, Reedy Creek Access
spots.notes_public: Small lake with a millstone marker from an old grist mill. Group campsites and a stone-deck picnic shelter.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Wilson Creek Gorge Kayak Put-In
spots.managing_agency: Pisgah National Forest / US Forest Service
spots.launch_type: Roadside pull-off with river bank access
spots.hazards: Wilson Creek Gorge contains Class II-IV whitewater — for experienced whitewater paddlers only. Water is cold year-round. Dress for immersion. Remote gorge with limited rescue access. River levels rise rapidly after rainfall.
spots.notes_public: A stunning whitewater put-in in the Wilson Creek Wild and Scenic River corridor in Pisgah National Forest. 4.8 stars across 64 reviews. The gorge is breathtaking — reviewers describe the scenery as absolutely beautiful with refreshing swimming holes.

spots.name: Worthville Road Access, Deep River
spots.managing_agency: Deep River Riverkeepers / Piedmont Legacy Trails
spots.ada_launch: Yes, two accessible parking spots. Concrete ramp.
spots.hazards: TWO DAMS DOWNSTREAM — NO PUBLIC TAKEOUTS BELOW THIS POINT. Central Falls Dam is 4.5 miles downstream — a 25-foot hydroelectric dam that is extremely dangerous. Exit LEFT near the hydroelectric building. Cedar Falls Dam follows at 5.8 miles. Class IV water just past Cedar Falls takeout can be deadly. This section is for experienced river paddlers only. Minimum recommended flow: 175 cfs on the USGS Deep River gauge.
spots.notes_public: Put-in 100 yards below Worthville Dam on the Deep River State Trail. Class I and II rapids through this stretch. Two mandatory dam portages downstream — Central Falls at 4.5 miles is 25 feet tall with steep banks.

spots.name: Wrightsville Beach Boating Access
spots.parking_spaces: Plenty for trailers, very limited car-only spaces
spots.fee_permit: Paid car parking nearby at $5/hour via smartphone app
spots.hazards: Heavy boat traffic and ICW currents. Tidal waters. Currents stronger than they appear. Check tide tables and plan accordingly.
spots.notes_public: The most centrally located launch on the Wrightsville Beach sound side. Access to the ICW, marsh creeks behind the island, and Banks Channel. Parking is genuinely difficult — reviewer waited over an hour for a space on a summer weekend.

spots.name: York Hill Yadkin River Access
spots.launch_type: Two access points: concrete boat ramp (#1) and hand-carry kayak steps (#2)
spots.camping_type: New campsites added as part of Yadkin River Park development
spots.notes_public: The most popular Yadkin River access in Davidson County and one of the most reviewed on the entire river. Technically sits at the upper end of High Rock Lake impoundment, so the water moves slowly — essentially flatwater despite being labeled a river access. Two access points: a concrete ramp for motorized boats and dedicated wooden steps for kayaks and canoes.
